title: Members' names on the device
text: Members' names on the device (spec 4.7, 5, 7). The device knows member ids (`added_by`, `checked_by`) but not their names: the edit sheet reads "Checked … by someone else". Add a local `household_member_names` table (`household_id`, `user_id`, `display_name`, `joined_at`; a cache that is never pushed, so it isn't in `mutate.ts` or the outbox). Fill it from `get_household_members` for each household after a full pull and whenever Realtime reports a membership change in a household, replacing that household's rows. Purge it with the household (`purge.ts`) and on sign-out and delete account (`wipeLocalData`). Add `memberName(householdId, userId)` and a live `useMemberNames(householdId)` in `src/features/households/`. They return the first word of the display name ("Alex" from "Alex Rivera"). When two members share a first word, add the last name's initial ("Alex R.", "Alex M."). An unknown, removed or null id returns "Someone" (*Alguien*). The current user is "You" (*Tú*). Use it in the edit sheet: "Checked 5 min ago by Alex" (spec 4.2's "by someone else" goes). Add `memberHue(userId)` built from `avatarColors` / `householdColor`, so a member has the same avatar colour everywhere. Tests: the cache fills from the RPC, is replaced on a membership event and is purged with the household; first-name and clash rules; the unknown and self fallbacks; the edit sheet's checked line for self, another member and a deleted user. Update spec 4.2, 4.7 and 5.
notes: Members' names on the device (2026-10-16, spec 4.7, 5): a local `household_member_names` cache (Drizzle `0020_household_member_names.sql`; no foreign keys, never pushed). `src/features/households/member-names.ts`: `refreshMemberNames` (replaces one household's rows from `get_household_members`; a failed call keeps them; never throws), `refreshAllMemberNames` (runs at the end of every full pull in `pull.ts`), `shortMemberNames` (the first word; "Alex R." / "Alex M." when first words clash), `nameOf` (You/Tú, the short name, or Someone/Alguien), `memberName(householdId, userId)` and the live `useMemberNames(householdId)`. Each household's Realtime channel now also listens to that household's `household_members` rows and reloads its names without a pull (a delete counts only for its own household). The cache is purged in `purgeHousehold` and `wipeLocalData`. `checkedLine` takes the household's names: "Checked 5 min ago by Alex", "… by someone" for an unknown or deleted user, "… by you" for the current user. New keys `addedBy.checkedBy`, `addedBy.checkedBySomeone` and `addedBy.someone`; `checkedBySomeoneElse` is gone. `memberHue(userId)` is in `aisle-color.ts` and colours the Households screen avatars (same hash as before, so colours don't change). Updated spec 4.2, 4.7 and 5. Tests: new `src/features/households/__tests__/member-names.test.ts` (16: fill, replace, a failure keeps the rows, null answer, refreshAll, first-name/clash/blank rules, You/Someone in English and Spanish, memberName, useMemberNames, memberHue); pull.test "members' names" (5: a full pull fills the cache, the next one replaces it, a scoped pull doesn't load names, a failure doesn't fail the pull, a lost household is purged with its names); realtime.test (2: join and leave events replace only that household's names); purge.test (1); item-screen.test (3: the checked line for the current user, another member and a deleted user). I changed existing tests where the behaviour changed: added-by.test and items-strings.test (the "someone else" checked line now names the member or says "someone"), realtime.test (household channel bindings now include `household_members`), and local-wipe.test (seeds the new table so the every-table wipe check covers it). `src/test/db.ts` now resets the new table. `yarn i18n:export` regenerated `docs/i18n/es-review.csv`, which also picked up about 90 strings earlier tasks hadn't exported. Jest 4045 passed (2 skipped); lint and tsc pass. No `supabase/` changes.

title: Last seen per list
text: Last seen per list (spec 4.1). Add the device setting `list.seenAt.<listId>`, a timestamp. It is set to now when the list stops being on screen after being shown in the foreground: switching lists, another tab, the app going to the background, the list deleted or archived. "On screen" uses the same rule as Keep screen on (4.1), so the list's own sheets count as on screen. A list opened for the first time on this device has no marker: set it at once, so it shows no card. Purge the settings with the household, like the other per-list device settings. Add `listNewsSince(listId, since)` in `src/features/lists/` (a live query) for the card. It returns, per other member, the live unchecked items on the list with a contribution that member added after `since` (a Combine into an existing item counts, and an item counts once however many contributions it has). Items and contributions added by you, by a null `added_by`, or by Siri on your account never count. Use the server `created_at` that pull stores. Allow 2 minutes of clock skew by counting from `since - 2 min`. Tests: the marker's set and not-set cases (sheet open, tab change, background); the first-open case; what counts (Combine, removed after adding, checked by me, my own adds from another device, null `added_by`); grouping per member; purge.
notes: Last seen per list (2026-10-16, spec 4.1): device setting `list.seenAt.<listId>` (ms; `listSeenAtKey` in `list-view.ts`). New `src/features/lists/last-seen.ts`: `getListSeenAt`, `markListSeen` (skips a list the device no longer has, so a screen closing after a purge leaves nothing behind), and `useListSeenMarker(listId, onScreen)`, wired into `ListScreen` with `shoppingOnList` (the Keep screen on rule). It marks a list shown for the first time at once, and marks it again whenever it stops being on screen in the foreground: another tab, a pushed screen or another list's sheet, the app backgrounded (not `inactive`), or the screen unmounting (switching lists, deleted, archived). `useForeground` is pulled out of `keep-awake.ts` for both hooks. `listNewsSince(listId, since, me = account)` is a re-runnable PromiseLike for `useLiveQueryOn(…, LIST_NEWS_QUERY_TABLES)`: live unchecked items with a live contribution from another member, created after `since - 2 min` (`SEEN_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`), grouped by `groupListNews` per member (each item once per member, dated by that member's latest add, newest first; members with the most items first, then the most recent). An item two members both added to is listed under both, so the card task should dedupe its total. `purgeHousehold` clears the markers. Tests: new `last-seen.test.tsx` (29: the marker set or not set for sheets, Your lists, a tab change, a pushed screen, another list's sheet, background vs inactive, never shown in the foreground, mounted off screen, first open, switching lists, deleted, archived, purged while shown, a bad stored value; news for a Combine, a repeated Combine counted once, the skew edge, an item removed, an amount removed, checked by me then unchecked, my adds from another device, Siri on my account, my Combine onto theirs, Siri on another member's account, null `added_by`, other lists, grouping and order, signed out, a re-run on each `then`), plus one purge test in `purge.test.ts`. Jest 4075 passed (2 skipped); lint and tsc pass. No spec text changed (the task didn't ask) and no `supabase/` changes.

title: The "since you looked" card and NEW rows
text: The "since you looked" card and NEW rows (spec 4.1; board 1 A). When a list opens with news (`listNewsSince` with its marker), a `Card` sits at the top of the list, above the first section, in every view mode. It has the members' avatars (up to 3, overlapping by 10 pt, in `memberHue`), a `headline` title, a `footnote` `inkSecondary` line and a ✕ (44 pt, VoiceOver "Dismiss"). Titles: "Alex added 4 items", "Alex and Sam added 7 items", "Alex, Sam and 2 others added 12 items". The `footnote` reads "Since you looked, yesterday at 6:40 PM", with *when* as the edit sheet's Added rows read it, plus a time. Under it, in `callout`, up to 3 names in sentence case, then "and 1 more". The card is worked out once when the list opens and doesn't change during the visit: items arriving live use the arrival cue, not the card. ✕ hides it for this visit. Each new item's row gets a `Badge` "NEW" (`primarySoft`) after the name, and a second line "Alex · yesterday" (the row's existing second line comes after it, e.g. "Alex · yesterday · from Chicken tacos"). The badges stay until the list stops being on screen, so moving the marker clears them. VoiceOver: the card is one element ("Alex added 4 items since yesterday, 6:40 PM: eggs, limes, corn tortillas and 1 more") with Dismiss as an action, and new rows add "new, added by Alex". Tests: each title form; names and "and N more"; frozen during the visit; dismiss; badges cleared after leaving and coming back; nothing at all for a list with no marker or no news; VoiceOver labels. Update spec 4.1. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: with two accounts in one household, add items on one device, open the list on the other, and check the card and the badges.
notes: The "since you looked" card and NEW rows (2026-10-16, spec 4.1): `useListSeenMarker` now also returns the current visit (`{ since, at, news }`): `listNewsSince` is read once as the list comes on screen with a marker, and the visit is cleared when the list leaves the screen, which moves the marker. New `src/features/lists/list-news.ts` has `summarizeNews` (an item counts once, under whoever added to it last), `newsTitle` (one, two, or "Alex, Sam and 2 others"), `newsSinceLine` ("Since you looked, yesterday at 6:40 PM"; under an hour just "5 min ago"), `newsItemsLine` (up to 3 names, the line in sentence case, then "and N more"), `newsCardLabel`, `rowNews` / `newRowLine` / `newRowLabel`, and `useListVisitNews` (✕ dismissal tied to the visit object). New `news-card.tsx` (`NewsCard`: avatars overlapping by 10 pt in `memberHue`, `headline` title, `footnote` line, `callout` names, a 44 pt ✕; one VoiceOver element with a Dismiss action). It's wired into `ListScreen` above the first section in every view mode, with `useMemberNames` for names. `ItemRow` takes `news`: a NEW `Badge` after the name, "Alex · yesterday" ahead of the second line, and "new, added by Alex" in its label after the name (`itemRowLabel` takes `news`). A new item checked off during the visit loses its badge. Strings are under `lists.news` in en/es (Spanish times are 24-hour, as `formatDate` gives for `es`). Added a spec 4.1 "Since you looked" bullet. I didn't re-run `yarn i18n:export`. Tests: new `list-news.test.ts` (17: each title form in English and Spanish, names and "and N more", the since line, summarize/dedupe/null, member names and Someone, row news, VoiceOver labels); `list-screen.test.tsx` "since you looked" (10: the card and rows in all three view modes, two members with ordering and avatars, frozen during the visit, ✕, the VoiceOver Dismiss action, cleared after leaving and showing only what's new on return, dismissal only for that visit, no marker, no news, a checked new item); `item-row.test.tsx` (2: badge, line and label; no news). Jest 4146 passed (2 skipped); lint and tsc pass. No `supabase/` changes. title: A row that arrives while you look
text: A row that arrives while you look (spec 4.1, 4.6; board 2 E, the prototype). While a list is on screen, an item that appears in its live query and that another member added (a new item, or a Combine raising an existing item's amount) gets an arrival cue. A new row grows into place: Reanimated `entering`/layout, about 250 ms. Under Reduce Motion it appears without growing. The row then gets the existing merge flash: `pendingSoft` fading to the row's tint over `motion` (reuse the add-merge flash and its timing, and add a `motion` token if one is missing). A `surface` name tag (radius `full`) sits before the amount: a 20 pt avatar in `memberHue` plus the first name ("Alex") in `caption` in the hue's `strong`. The tag stays until you scroll the list or leave it. If the row lands outside the visible area, a pill floats 8 pt above the add bar ("2 new from Alex", or "3 new" for several people, with a down arrow). Tapping it scrolls to the first such row, and it goes away once they've been seen. Your own adds and pull catch-up when a list first opens (items that existed before it was shown) never get the cue. No haptic and no sound. VoiceOver: an announcement, "Alex added limes", throttled to one per 5 s and grouped ("Alex added 3 items"). Tests: which changes get the cue (another member's add, a Combine, my add, the first load); the tag cleared by scrolling; the off-screen pill and its scroll; the Reduce Motion path; announcement grouping. Update spec 4.1. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on two devices, add items on one while watching the list on the other, in By aisle and As added, with Reduce Motion on and off.
notes: A row that arrives while you look (2026-10-16, spec 4.1): new `src/features/lists/arrivals.ts`. `useListArrivals(listId, items, onScreen, me)` keeps a visit per list (on screen by the Keep screen on rule, in the foreground). It starts from `readListContents`, a synchronous read of the list's live contribution ids and items to get, so a live query that loads late can't look like arrivals. It's worked out during render as the live query's rows change, so a new row mounts already knowing it arrived. `detectArrivals` picks items to get with a contribution not seen before, from another member (not me on any device, not a null `added_by`), made on the server after the visit started less `SEEN_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`, so pull catch-up doesn't count. `grow` is set when the item wasn't already to get (new, or a checked item re-added). It returns `cues` (flash and grow, for the visit), `tags` (cleared by `clearTags` on the FlatList's `onScrollBeginDrag`), `unseen` (for the pill, `markSeen`) and the latest batch for VoiceOver. Leaving the list clears all of it. `ItemContribution` now carries `addedBy` (`listItemsQuery` selects it). `ItemRow` takes `arrival` ({ key, grow }), `tag`, `arrivalRef` and `onArrivalLayout`. `arrival` uses `growIn`, a custom Reanimated entering in `use-motion.ts` that opens the height over `Motion.duration` and is skipped under Reduce Motion, and `ArrivalFlash`, a `pendingSoft` overlay that fades out over the new `Motion.flashMs` token and restarts on a new contribution key. `tag` is a `surface` pill before the amount: a 20 pt avatar (new `Sizes.tagAvatar`) in `memberHue` and the short name in `caption` in the hue's `strong`; the row label adds "added by Alex". `ListScreen` wraps the FlatList in a measured viewport view. Arrived rows are measured with `measureInWindow` after each arrival, layout and scroll (`inSight`: the row's middle is inside the list's frame; a row that isn't drawn, e.g. in a folded section, is out of sight). Rows out of sight show `ArrivalPill` 8 pt above the add bar ("2 new from Alex" / "3 new", `arrivalPillText`). It scrolls to the first in list order: centred, or opening the section and using `scrollToIndex` when the row isn't drawn. `useArrivalAnnouncements` announces at most once per `ANNOUNCE_EVERY_MS` (5 s): the first at once, then the rest grouped (`arrivalAnnouncement`: "Alex added limes", "Alex added 3 items", a sentence per member). What's waiting is dropped on leaving. No haptic. Strings are under `lists.arrivals` in en/es. The existing add-merge highlight (aisle `soft` while its toast shows) is unchanged; the arrival flash is its own fade with the new token. Spec 4.1 has a new "A row that arrives while you look" bullet; DESIGN.md has an "Arrival cue" entry. Tests: new `arrivals.test.ts` (20: another member's add, a Combine, my adds, null `added_by`, catch-up before the visit and the skew edge, a checked item, a checked item re-added grows, several amounts at once, signed out; `readListContents`; `inSight` edges; the pill for one member, several, none, Someone, Spanish; announcement wording, grouping, dedupe, several members, Spanish). `item-row.test.tsx` "an arrival" (8: grow and clip, the Reduce Motion path, a Combine doesn't grow, the flash colour and `flashMs` fade, a re-flash on a new key, the tag's look, order and label, no arrival, the ref and layout callbacks). Its Reanimated mock gained `useSharedValue`, `useAnimatedStyle`, `withTiming` and a Reduce Motion switch; no existing test changed. `list-screen.test.tsx` "a row that arrives while you look" (14: another member's add, a Combine, my adds, first load and pull catch-up, every view mode, the tag cleared by scrolling, leaving and the list's own sheets, background, a checked-off arrival, the off-screen pill counting, scrolling and clearing, a row landing in sight, a folded section opened by the pill, announcement throttle and grouping with no haptic, announcements dropped on leaving). Jest 4187 passed (2 skipped); lint and tsc pass. No `supabase/` changes. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on two devices, add items on one while watching the list on the other, in By aisle and As added, with Reduce Motion on and off (steps in manual-checks.md).

On B the row grows into place (about 250 ms; the rows below make room), flashes pale amber that fades to the row's colour, and shows a pill before the amount with A's coloured avatar and first name ("Alex"). On A, add an amount to an item already on the list ("2 milk"): on B that row flashes and gets the tag without growing. Scroll B's list by hand: the tags go. Add something on B itself: no cue. Scroll B so the top of the list is out of view, then add two items on A: a green pill "2 new from Alex ↓" floats 8 pt above the add bar (above the toast when one shows). Do all of this in By aisle and in As added, with Reduce Motion off and on (on: the row just appears, and still flashes). With VoiceOver on B: "Alex added limes" is spoken at once; three quick adds from A within 5 seconds give one more announcement, "Alex added 2 items"; no haptic or sound on any arrival.

title: "Alex is adding"
text: "Alex is adding" (spec 4.1, 7; board 2 D, the prototype). Use Supabase Realtime Presence on a private channel per open list, topic `list:<listId>`, separate from the sync channels, which have per-client topics. First read the current Supabase Realtime Authorization and Presence docs. A migration adds RLS policies on `realtime.messages` so that only members of the list's household can join that topic or track presence on it. While the list is on screen, the app is in the foreground and it's online, the app joins and tracks `{ user_id, adding }`. `adding` is true while the add field is focused and for 10 s after the person's last add. Updates are throttled to one a second. The app leaves the channel on leaving the list or going to the background. The list header shows a 32 pt pill under "9 to get · By aisle", on the green (a `HEADER_WASH` fill, `onHeader` text): a 24 pt avatar and "Alex is adding", or "Alex and Sam are adding", or "3 people are adding", with three dots that pulse (static under Reduce Motion). It fades in and out over 200 ms, ignores your own presence, and is hidden in add mode (the header is collapsed then). VoiceOver: the pill is a static text element, with no announcement. Presence never carries what is being typed. Tests: the presence state, joining and leaving (screen, background, offline); the 10 s tail and the throttle; the pill's text for 1, 2 and 3+ people; your own presence ignored; pgTAP that a non-member can't join the topic. Update spec 4.1 and 7. The user pushes the migration (hand them the command). NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on two devices, focus the add field on one and watch the header on the other; background the first and see the pill go.
notes: "Alex is adding" (2026-10-16, spec 4.1, 7.2): WebFetch wasn't permitted, so instead of the Supabase docs pages I read the installed realtime-js 2.117.3 (`private`, `presence.key`/`enabled`, `track`, `presenceState`, and how `channel()` reuses a topic) and the local `realtime` schema (`realtime.messages.topic`/`extension`, `realtime.topic()`). New migration `20261027153000_list_presence.sql`: `private.can_use_list_topic(topic)` (security definer: `list:<id>` for a list in one of the caller's households, compared as text) and two policies on `realtime.messages` for `authenticated`, select (join and receive) and insert (track), both only for `extension = 'presence'`. New `src/features/lists/presence.ts`: `othersAdding` (from presence state: each user once, in order, never me on any device), `addingPillText` (one, two, "3 people"), `createThrottle` (the first value at once, then the latest at most once per `PRESENCE_THROTTLE_MS`), `joinListPresence` (a private channel `list:<listId>` keyed by user; tracks `{ user_id, adding }` after SUBSCRIBED and again after a rejoin; a join waits for the last leave of the same topic, since realtime-js hands back an existing channel), `useListPresence` (joined while on screen by the Keep screen on rule, in the foreground and not offline, signed in and configured; leaving clears the pill) and `useAddingTail` (focused, or 10 s after the last add). `ListScreen` feeds it the add field's focus and calls `noteAdd` on an item add and a recipe add. New `adding-pill.tsx` (`AddingPill`): a `sizes.viewButton` pill in the new `listHeaderColors().presencePill` (`HEADER_WASH`, `onHeader`), with a 24 pt avatar (new `Sizes.presenceAvatar`), the text in `amount` and three 4 pt dots (`Sizes.presenceDot`) that pulse (`Motion.presencePulseMs`; still under Reduce Motion). It fades in and out over the new `Motion.presenceFadeMs` (200), has `accessibilityRole="text"`, no live region and no announcement, and is `hidden` in add mode. It sits inside the collapsing header, under the count and view button. Strings are under `lists.presence` in en/es. Spec 4.1 has an "Alex is adding" bullet, 7.2 a "List presence" bullet, and DESIGN.md an "Adding pill" entry. `fake-supabase` channels now record `opts`, `track` payloads and presence listeners, with `setPresence`. The list-screen test's Reanimated mock gained `withDelay`/`withRepeat`/`withSequence`; no existing test changed. title: The eval first: can a model match ingredients to steps?
text: The eval first: can a model match ingredients to steps? (spec 6; `docs/spikes.md`). Add an AI task `match-recipe-steps` in `_shared/ai/tasks.ts`, with a versioned prompt (`prompts/match-recipe-steps.v1.ts`) and `AI_MODEL_STEPS` (default the recipe model; optional `_FALLBACK`). Input: the steps (numbered) and the ingredients (numbered: name, quantity, unit, note). Output (Zod): for each step, a list of `{ ingredient: <index>, quantity: number | null }`, where `quantity` is that step's share in the ingredient's own unit when the recipe splits it ("juice of 1 lime" from 3 limes), and null for all of it or not stated. Validation drops unknown indexes and repeats within a step, nulls a share that isn't positive or is over the total, and turns a step count that doesn't match into `unavailable`. The prompt: the recipe is untrusted text; only ingredients the step actually uses; "the chicken" in step 5 means the cooked chicken from step 1, which is not a new use; a pantry staple named in no step stays unplaced. Add the eval at `supabase/functions/match-recipe-steps/eval/`: 15 or more recipes from the import eval's fixtures that have steps, with hand-labelled expected matches in `expected.json`. `yarn ai:eval:steps [--model …]` prints per-recipe and overall precision and recall of (step, ingredient) pairs, the share of ingredients placed nowhere, split-amount accuracy, and median and p95 latency and cost per recipe. Run it on the current recipe model and on at least one cheaper model. Also add `yarn ai:steps` for trying one recipe by hand, like `yarn ai:tags`, with an in-memory store and the real model unless `--model mock`. It accepts a recipe link (`yarn ai:steps https://…`: the import's own fetch and extraction get the steps and ingredients, with nothing cached or written), `--file page.html`, or `--step "…"` and `--ingredient "2 lb chicken thighs"` flags, repeated, for a recipe typed in. It prints each numbered step, then its matched ingredients indented under it with amounts and shares ("Limes · 1 of 3"), then "Not in a step" with the unplaced ones, then the model, the prompt version, the latency and the tokens. It also takes `--model`, `--raw` (the model's JSON as returned), `--json` and `--quiet`, as `ai:tags` does. Document both scripts in `docs/llm-calls.md` "Running a call yourself". Write the results and a go/no-go with the chosen model in `docs/spikes.md` §5 ("Step ingredients"). Suggested bar: precision ≥ 0.95 (a wrong ingredient on a step is worse than a missing one) and recall ≥ 0.85. No app or database changes in this task. Tests: the schema and validation (bad index, repeat, a share over the total, step count mismatch); the mock model, which matches by name words appearing in the step text; the eval scorer on a tiny fixture. If the bar isn't met, mark this done, write up why in the spikes doc, and stop: tell the user in progress.md that the rest of the section is on hold.
notes: The eval first: step ingredients (2026-10-16, spec 4.5, 6; docs/spikes.md §5): **done, go.** New AI task `matchRecipeSteps` in `_shared/ai/tasks.ts` (`AI_MODEL_STEPS`, else `AI_MODEL_RECIPE`, fallbacks likewise; `AI_THINKING_STEPS`; 20 s timeout; `stepsMaxOutputTokens` 200 + 80 per step, capped at 6,000) with `MatchRecipeStepsOutputSchema` and `cleanStepMatch` (steps that don't line up → null, which `matchRecipeSteps` throws as `steps_mismatch`; unknown or repeated ingredients dropped; a share is kept only when positive and below the ingredient's quantity, rounded to 3 decimals; uses in recipe order). Prompt `prompts/match-recipe-steps.v1.ts`, its rules in `prompts/step-match-rules.ts` for the later import task. Mock `mockStepsModel` (an ingredient's last name word in the step text). `supabase/functions/match-recipe-steps/`: `match.ts` (`matchRecipeSteps`, `StepMatchRecipeSchema`, `StepMatchError`; no index.ts yet, the Edge Function is a later task), `cli.ts` (`yarn ai:steps <url>`, `--file`, or `--step`/`--ingredient`; a link or file goes through `importRecipe` with categorize on the mock), `eval/eval.ts` (`yarn ai:eval:steps`, `--only`, `--price-in`/`--price-out`) and `eval/recipes.json` (16 recipes: 13 import-eval JSON-LD pages with the import model's ingredients frozen in, plus typed tacos with split limes, Spanish sopa de fideo, and an injection step; 100 steps, 220 needed pairs, hand-labelled). Results: gemini-3.8-flash 100% precision, 100% recall, all shares right, p50 2.5 s / p95 8.0 s; gemini-3.5-flash-lite 99.1% / 100%, p50 1.2 s / p95 2.0 s; ~1,000 in / 200 out tokens per recipe. Decision: keep `AI_MODEL_STEPS` unset (follows the recipe model). Docs: `docs/llm-calls.md`, `docs/spikes.md` §5, `.env.example`. Tests: 27 new Deno tests in `match-recipe-steps` pass; suggest-recipe-tags (58), import-recipe (119) and categorize-ingredients (290) still pass; `yarn tsc` and `yarn expo lint` clean.

title: Saving the match on the recipe
text: Saving the match on the recipe (spec 5, 7). A migration adds `recipes.step_ingredients jsonb` (null = never matched). Shape: `{ "v": 1, "basis": "<hash>", "steps": [[{ "id": "<recipe_ingredient_id>", "quantity": null }], …] }`, one entry per step. A shape check (`private.recipe_step_ingredients_ok`, like the steps check) allows at most 100 steps and 80 ids per step, and needs `v` and `basis`. The ids aren't checked against `recipe_ingredients`, because deleted ones are filtered in the app. `apply_mutation` takes it as a last-writer-wins field, the whole value as one field like `tags` (a new migration redefining `private.apply_mutation` from the latest one). Add it to the local schema (Drizzle migration), `mutate.ts`, push and pull (compared by content, like `tags`). Add the pure `stepIngredientsBasis(steps, liveIngredientIds)` in `src/shared/` (a stable hash of the step texts and the sorted ids). Add `stepMatch(recipe, ingredients)` in `src/features/recipes/`. It returns `{ state: 'none' | 'fresh' | 'stale', steps: [...], unplaced: [...] }`, where `steps` has the live ingredients for each step (deleted ids dropped, the rest in the recipe's ingredient order) and `unplaced` has the live ingredients in no step. The match is stale when the basis doesn't match. A stale match is still shown. Tests: the basis is stable across key order and changes with a step edit, an added ingredient and a deleted ingredient; deleted ids are filtered; unplaced; the shape check accepts good values and refuses bad ones (pgTAP); a pull round-trip. The user pushes the migrations (hand them the command).
notes: Saving the step match on the recipe (2026-10-16, spec 4.5, 5, 7): Supabase migration `20261025120000_step_ingredients.sql` adds `recipes.step_ingredients jsonb` with `private.recipe_step_ingredients_ok` (an object with a positive-integer `v`, a 1–64-char `basis` and 1–100 steps of at most 80 `{ id: 1–64 chars, quantity: null or > 0 }`; written with cases so a value of the wrong type is refused, not thrown on). I did NOT redefine `private.apply_mutation`, though the task asked for it: `recipes` has no settable-column list there (every column that isn't a key or the server's is settable, as `recipe_steps.sql` notes), so the column is already field-level LWW as one value, and the pgTAP test shows it. Copying the 260-line function unchanged would only risk merge conflicts. Local: `recipes.stepIngredients` + Drizzle `0019_step_ingredients.sql`. mutate, push and pull needed no code change: they handle columns generically, and pull's `canonicalJson` already compares jsonb by content. `src/shared/step-ingredients.ts`: the `StepIngredients` type and `stepIngredientsBasis` (a cyrb53 hex hash of JSON [steps, sorted ids]). `src/features/recipes/step-match.ts`: `stepMatch` (none/fresh/stale; live ingredients ordered by position; deleted and unknown ids dropped; a repeated id counted once; shares kept; steps line up with the recipe's current steps). title: The `match-recipe-steps` Edge Function
text: The `match-recipe-steps` Edge Function (spec 6, 4.12). It takes a JWT-authenticated `POST { steps, ingredients: [{ id, name, quantity, unit, note }] }` (the schema in `src/shared/schemas/`, shared with the app). It validates (`400`, `413` over 256 KB) and checks a new feature `step_ingredients` (`403 not_entitled`). The migration seeds the feature on standard and plus, and the pgTAP plan checks cover it. It checks `AI_MODEL_STEPS=off` (`503`), then per-user limits (30 a minute, 300 a day; `check_step_match_limit`, like the tag limit) and a global daily cap `STEP_MATCH_DAILY_CAP` (default 5,000). It makes one call with the chosen model from the eval, `temperature: 0`, a 20 s timeout and `maxOutputTokens` sized from the eval, and maps the indexes back to the request's ids. It returns `200 { steps, promptVersion }` and stores nothing but `ai_calls`. Errors, input caps and the `Retry-After` values are as `suggest-recipe-tags` has them. `yarn ai:steps` (from the eval task) now runs through this handler. Tests (Deno): validation, entitlement before limits, limits, the off switch, id mapping, the mock model end to end. Update spec 6 (a new 6.8) and 4.12, and `docs/llm-calls.md`. The user deploys the function and sets the secrets (hand them the commands).

Shared schema `src/shared/schemas/match-recipe-steps.ts` (`MatchRecipeStepsRequestSchema`: 1–100 steps, at least one not blank, trimmed and cut to 2,000; ingredients with unique 1–64-char ids, empty names dropped, first 80, at least one; response `{ steps: [[{ id, quantity }]], promptVersion }`). Function `supabase/functions/match-recipe-steps/`: `handler.ts` (`matchSteps`: plan → off switch → limits → `matchRecipeSteps`; blank steps not sent and answered `[]`; indexes mapped back to ids; steps_mismatch is a 503 with Retry-After 30), `request.ts` (400/405/413/500 not_configured/503 as suggest-recipe-tags; `STEP_MATCH_DAILY_CAP` default 5,000), `store.ts`, `index.ts`. `yarn ai:steps` now runs `matchSteps` against `MemoryStepMatchStore` (ids "1", "2", …); its `--json` now prints `{ name, source, request, response }`, so I changed the existing cli.test `--json` assertion to match. `Feature` gains `step_ingredients` in `_shared/entitlements.ts` and in the app's `FEATURES` (so `my_features` keeps it). I left the app's `DEFAULT_FEATURES` as `['categorize']` although standard now also has `step_ingredients`: the next task (`ensureStepMatch`) should decide whether to add it. I changed the existing `17_plans.test.sql` for the new feature (seeded rows, my_features answers; plan 42 → 46). title: Matching recipes in the background
text: Matching recipes in the background (spec 4.5). Add `ensureStepMatch(recipeId)` in `src/features/recipes/`. It does nothing when offline, when the user lacks `step_ingredients`, when the recipe has no steps or no ingredients, when the match is `fresh`, or when a call for that recipe is already in flight. Otherwise it calls the function and, if the recipe's basis is unchanged when the answer comes back, writes `step_ingredients` through `mutate.ts`. Call it after a recipe import saves, after the Steps sheet's Save, 2 s after the last ingredient edit on the recipe screen, and when the recipe screen or the cook screen opens (which is how recipes from before this feature get matched; there's no launch backfill). Errors are silent, with no UI. `unavailable` and `rate-limited` pause all matching for an hour (in memory), and `not-entitled` stops it for the session. Two household devices may both match; the last writer wins, which is fine. Tests: each skip condition; a basis change during the call drops the answer; each trigger, including opening a recipe that has steps but no match; the pauses.
notes: Matching recipes in the background (2026-10-16, spec 4.5): added `src/features/recipes/ensure-step-match.ts` with `ensureStepMatch(recipeId)` (skips when paused/stopped, without `step_ingredients`, with no non-blank steps or no live ingredients, a fresh match, offline/signed out, and joins a call already in flight for that recipe; writes `step_ingredients` via `updateRows` only if the basis is unchanged when the answer returns), `ensureStepMatchSoon` (2 s debounce per recipe) and `useEnsureStepMatch`. `unavailable`/`rate_limited` (or a bare 503/429) pause all matching for an hour; `not_entitled` (or a bare 403) stops it for the session and calls `lostFeature`; all errors are silent. Triggers: `importRecipe` after it saves, the Steps sheet's Save, recipe-screen ingredient add/edit/delete/undo (debounced), and opening the recipe and cook screens. Exported `knownOffline` from `suggest-tags.ts` so both callers share it. Added a 4.5 bullet to the spec. Tests: `ensure-step-match.test.ts` (31: the request and saved value, shares, stale re-match, each skip, in-flight join, a basis change during the call drops the answer (step edit, added/deleted ingredient, deleted recipe; a rename keeps it), wrong step count/malformed/thrown/network/500 are silent with no pause, the hour pause for each code, the session stop, the 2 s debounce per recipe, the import trigger) and `step-match-triggers.test.tsx` (11: opening the recipe and cook screens with steps but no match, no steps, fresh, no feature; Steps sheet Save; recipe-screen add, delete, delete+undo). jest 4058 passed (2 skipped); lint and tsc pass.

title: Imports come back already matched
text: Imports come back already matched (spec 6.6, 4.10). Add `extract-recipe.v4.ts`, keeping v3's file with a byte-for-byte test as v2 has. v4 also returns `step_ingredients`: for each output step, `{ ingredient: <index into the output ingredients>, quantity: number | null }`, using the matching rules from `match-recipe-steps.v1` (share the rule text in a `_shared/ai/prompts/step-match-rules.ts` that both prompts import). Today the JSON-LD path sends only ingredient lines, and the steps come from JSON-LD after the call. In v4, the JSON-LD steps (after `cleanRecipeSteps`) are sent to the model too, numbered, as untrusted data, with "match these, don't rewrite them". The model still returns `steps: []` for them, and the server keeps the JSON-LD steps. The page-text path matches the steps it extracts. Validate the result as `match-recipe-steps` does. A step count that doesn't match the final steps, or any invalid match, drops `step_ingredients` and keeps the rest of the import: a bad match never fails an import. `RecipeImportResponse` gains `stepIngredients: [[{ index, quantity }]] | null` (indexes into the response's `ingredients`). An older server's response without it reads as null. When the import creates the recipe, the app saves it as `step_ingredients`, mapping indexes to the new `recipe_ingredients` ids, with the basis worked out from what it saved. That makes the match fresh, so `ensureStepMatch` makes no call. A reused recipe keeps its own match, the same rule as tags (4.14). The prompt version is in the cache key, so v3 results aren't served. Re-run `yarn ai:eval:recipe` (ingredients, tags and steps must not get worse) and add the step-match score from the steps eval to it. Note in `docs/spikes.md` §5 whether matching inside the import is as good as the standalone call; if it's clearly worse, set `step_ingredients` to null in the response and leave matching to `ensureStepMatch`. Raise `maxOutputTokens` to fit. `yarn ai:recipe` prints the import's step match under its ingredient table, in `ai:steps`' format. Tests (Deno): v4 sends JSON-LD steps and keeps them; the match maps to the output ingredients; a bad match is dropped and the import still succeeds; the mock returns a match. In the app: an import saves a fresh match and makes no `match-recipe-steps` call; null leaves the recipe unmatched; a reused recipe isn't changed. Update spec 6.6 and 4.10. The user deploys the function (hand them the command).

title: Cook mode with ingredients under each step
text: Cook mode with ingredients under each step (spec 4.5; board 3 G and I, board 4 L). When `stepMatch` isn't `none`, the cook screen changes in four ways. (1) The Ingredients card becomes **All ingredients**, folded by default, one row with a "9 · 5 ticked" `footnote` and a chevron. It unfolds to today's checklist and stays as set for this visit. (2) Each step in the Method card lists its ingredients under its text in a rounded (`md`) inset on `background` (`surface` on the UP NEXT step's `primarySoft`). Each is a row of at least 44 pt: a 22 pt check, the name in `cookStep`, and the amount (`amount` `inkSecondary`) scaled to the servings as today. A split share shows its own scaled amount followed by "of 3" ("1 of 3"); for a split with no share, the amount is followed by "part". A step with no ingredients shows none. (3) An **Also needed** card after Method, headed "Not in a step", lists the unplaced ingredients. (4) Ticks are per (step, ingredient): ticking a step ticks its ingredients (unticking the step leaves them). An All ingredients row is ticked when every one of its uses is ticked, and ticking it there ticks all its uses. The counts follow. With no match, the screen is exactly today's. Ticks are still the screen's state only. VoiceOver: step rows keep their label and add "uses chicken thighs, chipotle in adobo, limes, garlic". Ingredient rows read "<name>, <amount>, for step 1", or ", 1 of 3 limes". Tests: the matched and unmatched layouts; the fold; split amounts with servings scaling; the tick rules both ways; Also needed; VoiceOver labels; the `stale` state still shows the match. title: No chips while the add field is empty
text: No chips while the add field is empty (spec 4.2). Today an empty, focused add field on a list shows the household's usual items in the chip row. Stop that: with the field empty (whitespace counts), there's no chip row at all, on lists as on recipes. Chips appear only once something is typed, as autocomplete, exactly as now. title: Shortest match first in autocomplete
text: Shortest match first in autocomplete (spec 4.2). Typing `coffee` on a list shows "Coffee filters" before "Coffee": `rankHistory` (`src/domain/suggestion-rank.ts`) sorts by frecency first, and `getSuggestions` (`src/features/lists/suggestions.ts`) puts every history match ahead of the catalog. Change the order of the item chips. (1) A suggestion whose name is the typed name (both normalized as an add, so `coffees` counts too) comes first, from history or the catalog. With 2 or more history matches the catalog is still left out, except for this exact match, which always shows. (2) Then shorter names before longer ones, whether they come from history or the catalog. (3) At equal length, a whole-name prefix match beats a word match, then higher frecency, then history before catalog, then alphabetical. The limit (5), the dedupe by key and recipe chips leading the row don't change. Tests: `coffee` with history Coffee filters (often bought) and Coffee gives Coffee, then Coffee filters. Coffee only in the catalog with two history matches still shows Coffee first. `chi` gives Chives before Chicken thighs. Also cover the tie-breaks. Update spec 4.2's **Ranking** bullet and the JSDoc on `rankHistory` and `getSuggestions`.
notes: Shortest match first in autocomplete (2026-10-16, spec 4.2): `suggestion-rank.ts` gets `matchSuggestion` (exact when a name is the typed name, both through `normalizeIngredientName`, so `coffees` is Coffee; else prefix/word as before) and `compareMatches` (exact, then shorter display name, then prefix before word). `rankHistory` sorts by that, then frecency, then alphabetical, and also matches a row that is the typed name. New `mergeSuggestions(history, catalog, query, limit)` orders both sources the same way, then history (in `rankHistory` order) before the catalog, then alphabetical; dedupe by key (history wins) and the limit unchanged. `searchRecentItems` also pre-filters on the key being the typed name's. New `catalogEntry(name)` in `categories.ts` looks up the catalog grocery row for the typed name; `getSuggestions` always includes it, while with 2+ history matches the rest of the catalog is still left out. JSDoc on `rankHistory`, `getSuggestions`, `searchRecentItems` and `suggestionChips` updated; spec 4.2 **Ranking** rewritten and **History first** notes the exact-match exception. Existing tests changed because the order changed: suggestion-rank.test.ts (the two frecency tests use equal-length names; "prefix ahead of word" and "higher-scoring word beats prefix" became "at equal length prefix beats a higher-scoring word match" and "a shorter word match beats a longer prefix match"), items.test.ts "applies the limit after ranking" (now chili, chive), suggestions.test.ts (one-history-match/dedupe, hidden rows, applySuggestion, hide-drops-below-2 use queries/expectations for the new order), categories.test.ts autocomplete (adds `chickens`). New tests: rankHistory (4: typed name first however often others are bought, plural and accent exact, exact beats a shorter match, `chi` Chili/Chives before Chicken thighs); `mergeSuggestions` (7: exact from the catalog and as a plural, shorter first across sources, prefix before word at equal length, history order then catalog alphabetical, dedupe, limit, no match/blank); searchRecentItems (exact key first, `coffees`); getSuggestions (5: Coffee before often-bought Coffee filters, `coffees`, an amount; catalog Coffee first with two history matches and `Coffees`; `chi` Chives before Chicken thighs; shorter catalog names before a longer history name with the 14-letter tie going to history, and the limit; history before catalog at equal length). Jest 4237 passed (2 skipped); lint and tsc pass. No `supabase/` changes. title: Drag to reorder in As added doesn't move rows live
text: Drag to reorder in As added doesn't move rows live (spec 4.6 "Your own order"). Long-pressing a row in As added and dragging it doesn't really work: the other rows never make room while you drag, so the list doesn't rearrange under the finger as it should (as the Aisle order screen does, board 12). Find out why in `src/features/lists/reorderable-rows.tsx` and `row-drag.ts` (e.g. the row boxes not being measured or kept up to date inside the FlatList, the shift styles not reacting to `to`, the long-press and pan not handing off, or the list's own scroll or swipe gestures taking the touch) and fix it so the spec's behaviour holds: the row lifts (bigger, with a shadow), the others slide to make room as it passes them, the list scrolls near its edges, and the drop lands where the gap is and saves once (no jump back, no saving when dropped in place). Long-press and lift without moving still enters Select mode, and tap and swipe are unchanged. Tests: the pure drag math in `row-drag.ts` for moving up and down past several rows and across a scroll; whatever the cause turned out to be, covered so it can't come back. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on a device, in As added on a list with 10+ items, drag a row up and down several places (and far enough to auto-scroll) and check the others make room live and the drop lands and stays where you let go.
notes: Drag to reorder in As added moves rows live (2026-10-16, spec 4.6): the cause was each row's `onLayout` doing `boxes.set({ ...boxes.get(), [id]: box })` on the JS thread. In Reanimated 4.5 a JS-thread `set` is only scheduled onto the UI thread while `get` reads the UI value now, so rows laying out together overwrote one another and only the last row's box survived. The rest counted as zero height, so nothing made room and the drop slots were wrong. Fix: `boxes.modify(all => withBox(all, id, box))`, which runs in order on the UI thread. Also pulled the drag reaction's math into a pure `dragTo(rows, from, translation, scrolled)` in `row-drag.ts`, placed below `clampDrag` because the worklets plugin turns worklet functions into consts, which aren't hoisted. Tests: `row-drag.test.ts` adds `dragTo` (down and up past several rows including a taller one, across an auto-scroll both ways, clamped at the ends, no boxes) and `withBox`. `reorderable-rows.test.tsx`'s Reanimated mock now defers JS-thread `set`/`modify` until the UI thread runs, as on device (an existing test file's mock changed, no assertions weakened), and adds two tests that the other rows make room live, down and up. Those two tests and two existing drop tests fail with the old `onLayout`. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK (in manual-checks.md).
manualChecks: Drag to reorder in As added moves rows live: on a device, in As added on a list with 10+ items (a few with notes, so rows differ in height), long-press a row and drag it up and down several places, and far enough to auto-scroll at the top and bottom edges. Check that the row lifts (bigger, with a shadow), the others slide to make room as it passes them, and the drop lands where the gap was and stays there with no jump back. A long-press let go without moving should enter Select mode; dropping a row back in its own place shouldn't change anything; tap and swipe should work as before.

title: A longer chain of photo fallbacks in `import-recipe`
text:
A longer chain of photo fallbacks in `import-recipe` (spec 6.6 step 5, `src/shared/recipe-jsonld.ts`, `supabase/functions/_shared/fetch-page.ts`). The photo is the first usable one of, in order: (1) the JSON-LD Recipe's `image`, now also resolving an `{ "@id": … }` reference to an `ImageObject` elsewhere in the same `@graph` (the Yoast/WordPress pattern, which today yields nothing), and `thumbnailUrl`; (2) the `@graph`'s `WebPage` `primaryImageOfPage` or `Article` `image` (same `@id` resolution); (3) `og:image`, `og:image:secure_url`, `og:image:url`; (4) `twitter:image`, `twitter:image:src`; (5) ``; (6) microdata `itemprop="image"` (`content`, `src` or `href`); (7) the first content `` inside `
` or `
` (else the body) that looks like a photo: skip `svg`, `gif`, `data:` URLs, tracking pixels and anything whose `src`, `class`, `id` or `alt` says logo, avatar, icon, sprite, badge, ad or gravatar, and skip images with a declared `width` or `height` under 300; read `src`, else `data-src`, `data-lazy-src`, `data-original`, else the largest `srcset`/`data-srcset` candidate. Every candidate still goes through `cleanImageUrl` (https, ≤ 2048, resolved against the page). The client-sent page path (`request.page.imageUrl`) gets the same chain where it has the markup. Bump nothing in the prompt; the photo is never read by the model. Add a `readImageCandidates(markup, jsonLd, pageUrl)` that returns the ordered, de-duplicated list (up to 12) and use its first entry as `image_url`; the next task reuses it. Tests in `recipe-jsonld.test.ts`, `fetch-page.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`: one per rung, the `@id` reference, lazy-loaded `data-src`/`srcset`, logo/avatar/pixel/small images skipped, order (an earlier rung wins), de-duplication, and a page with nothing still gives null. Add a fixture page for the cottage cheese blueberry bread recipe (URL: https://snacks.webxo.xyz/high-protein-cottage-cheese-blueberry-bread/) to `supabase/functions/import-recipe/eval/fixtures/` if one doesn't exist, and a test that it now gets a photo. Note: on 2026-10-16 that page, fetched with `fetch-page.ts`'s `USER_AGENT`, had an `og:image` (`…/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Screenshot-2026-03-23-112812.png`, a PNG) and a Yoast `@graph` with no Recipe node, and today's `readPage` already returns that og:image for it, so the fixture test alone would pass before this task's changes. Find where the photo was actually lost and cover that with a test too. Suspects: the client-sent page path (`page-capture.ts` → `request.page.imageUrl`), the app saving or reusing a recipe by URL in `src/features/recipes/import.ts` without taking `imageUrl`, a cached extraction (`getCached`) from before og:image was read, and the photo failing to load in the app (`usePhotoFailed`). Say in progress.md which one it was; if none of them reproduces, say so. Update spec 6.6 step 5's **Photo** sentence with the chain.
notes: A longer chain of photo fallbacks in import-recipe (2026-10-16, spec 6.6 step 5): `jsonLdImageCandidates(blocks, pageUrl)` in `src/shared/recipe-jsonld.ts` (rung 1 the Recipe's `image` then `thumbnailUrl`, rung 2 `WebPage` `primaryImageOfPage` then `Article` `image`, `{ "@id" }` references resolved across every block, one hop, no loops); `findRecipe`'s `imageUrl` resolves `@id` and falls back to `thumbnailUrl` too. `readImageCandidates(markup, jsonLd, pageUrl)` in `_shared/fetch-page.ts` adds og:image/secure_url/url, twitter:image/src (on `property` or `name`), ``, microdata `itemprop="image"` and the first content `` (article, else main, else body; logo/avatar/icon/sprite/badge/ad/gravatar/pixel words in src/class/id/alt, declared px size under 300, svg/gif/`data:` skipped; `src`, `data-src`, `data-lazy-src`, `data-original`, largest `srcset`/`data-srcset` via the new `largestSrcsetUrl`), de-duplicated, at most 12. `readPage` returns them as `imageCandidates` with `imageUrl` the first. The client-page path uses `clientPageImage` (JSON-LD rungs from the sent blocks, then the sent `imageUrl`). **Where the photo was lost: the client-sent page path, from Safari's share sheet.** `targets/share-recipe/Preprocess.js` never captured an image, and `ShareQueue.Envelope.Page` had no `imageUrl`, so a Safari share sent `{ title, jsonLd, text }`; the server uses a sent page without fetching, and with a Yoast `@graph` that has no Recipe node the photo was null although the page had an og:image. Fixed both ways: the server now reads the `@graph`'s primary image, and Preprocess.js, `CAPTURE_SCRIPT` (both from the new `PAGE_IMAGE_SOURCES`, rungs 3–6) and the Swift `ShareQueue.page(…, imageUrl:)` / `ShareViewController` now send it. The other suspects don't reproduce: the device fallback for pasted links (`page-capture.ts`) already sent og:image; `getCached` is keyed by prompt version and og:image reading shipped with v3, so no cached row predates it; `import.ts` reusing a recipe by URL keeps that recipe's own fields by design (a recipe first saved without a photo stays so, as its tags do), which isn't this page's first import; `usePhotoFailed` can't be checked without a device. Rung 7 (content ``) is server-only; the device doesn't run it. The Swift edits weren't compiled (no build here). **The fixture `nojsonld-webxo-cottage-cheese-blueberry-bread.html` is a hand reconstruction**: curl and WebFetch were blocked in this session, so it was built from the task's description (Yoast @graph without Recipe, that og:image PNG) with made-up recipe text, logo, avatars and a lazy ``; SOURCES.md says so, and manual-checks.md has the command to replace it. Tests: recipe-jsonld.test.ts (@id in the same graph, after the Recipe, in another block, self/bad references, thumbnailUrl; `jsonLdImageCandidates` rungs 1–2, IRI/array types, order, dedupe, Recipe without ingredients, malformed blocks, no page URL); fetch-page.test.ts (one test per rung 1–7, lazy attributes and srcset, 20 skipped logo/avatar/pixel/small/svg/gif/data/http cases plus near-misses like "silicone", order across all seven rungs, dedupe after cleaning, the 12 cap, nothing usable → [] and null, the cottage fixture); handler.test.ts (the fixture fetched gets the photo and caches it; **the regression: a Safari-shaped page from the fixture with no imageUrl gets the photo**; JSON-LD photos before a sent imageUrl; a lazy-only page; a Recipe `@id` image beats og:image); page-capture.test.ts (the rest of the tag chain in order, `PAGE_IMAGE_SOURCES`); share-extension.test.ts (Preprocess.js returns og:image, the fallback order, its list equals `PAGE_IMAGE_SOURCES`, an over-long URL left out). Existing tests changed because behavior changed: fetch-page.test.ts's full-shape `fetchPage` assertion gains `imageCandidates: []`, and "Other tags and meta keys are not the image" no longer expects `name="og:image"` and `` to be ignored; share-extension.test.ts's Preprocess.js results gain `imageUrl: ''` (its fake document gained `querySelector`); page-capture.test.ts's fake `querySelector` takes attribute objects; eval.test.ts counts go from 20 to 21 pages (5 without JSON-LD, is_recipe 20/21 (95.2%), 21 calls, 19 tagged pages) for the new fixture. Spec 6.6 (request `imageUrl`, step 4, step 5's **Photo**) updated. jest 4269 passed, Deno import-recipe 152, fetch-page 58, match-recipe-steps 60, lint and tsc clean, db reset and pgTAP 945 pass. Deploy: `supabase functions deploy import-recipe`; the share extension needs a new build. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: replace the fixture with the real page and share it from Safari on a device (manual-checks.md).

(2) After `supabase functions deploy import-recipe` and a dev build with the new share extension (the Swift edits weren't compiled here), share that page from Safari (Share → The Perfect Bite) and check the imported recipe shows the bread photo. Do the same with a pasted link to it. Also import a page whose only photo is a lazy-loaded one in the article (no og:image) and check it gets one.

title: Choose a recipe's photo

On the recipe screen, a recipe with no photo shows a dashed "Add photo" tile in the header band where the photo would be, and the recipe's menu gains **Change photo…** when it has one. Either opens a **Choose a photo** sheet: (1) **From the page**, only when the recipe's link opens: a grid of up to 12 candidates (4:3 tiles, the selected one with a `primary` border), loaded on open from a new `recipe-photos` Edge Function (JWT, `POST { url }` → `{ images: string[] }`) that fetches the page with `fetchPage` and returns `readImageCandidates` (rate limited like `import-recipe`; no AI call, no plan feature needed; `fetch_failed` and an empty list show "No photos found on the page"). title: Photos from your library or camera
text: Photos from your library or camera (spec 4.5, 5). Add `expo-image-picker` and `expo-image-manipulator` with `yarn expo install` (read the SDK's versioned docs first; add the photo library and camera usage strings in `app.json` through the config plugin). (1) **Storage.** A new migration adds a **private** Storage bucket `recipe-photos` (also in `supabase/config.toml` for local): objects at `<household_id>/<recipe_id>/<uuid>.jpg`, jpeg only, 2 MB cap. RLS on `storage.objects` lets a member of that household select, insert and delete under its prefix (the first folder, via `storage.foldername`) and nobody else; no update, since a new photo is a new object. (2) **Data.** A new synced column `recipes.photo_path text` (null = none), checked against that path shape with its household prefix equal to the recipe's `household_id`, merged per field through `field_clock` like the other recipe columns, in `src/db/schema.ts`, the sync pull and push, and the outbox. `image_url` keeps the site's photo and its https check unchanged. The photo shown is `photo_path` when set, else `image_url`. (3) **Showing it.** `recipePhotoSource(recipe, session)` (`src/features/recipes/`) returns the `expo-image` source: for `photo_path`, `{ uri: <SUPABASE_URL>/storage/v1/object/authenticated/recipe-photos/<path>, headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <access token>' }, cacheKey: <path> }`, so the disk cache is keyed by path and survives token refreshes and offline use; otherwise `image_url` as today. If a load fails with 400/401/403, refresh the session and retry once before falling back to the icon tile (`usePhotoFailed`). First confirm in the SDK's `expo-image` docs that `headers` is sent on iOS and Android; if it isn't, use signed URLs instead (`createSignedUrls` in one call per screen, 7 days, cached in memory per path and renewed before expiry, same `cacheKey`) and say so in progress.md. `RecipePhotoTile`, `RecipePhotoCover` and the recipe screen's header all use it, and every caller that passes a recipe's `image_url` today passes `photo_path` too (the plan grid's entries in `week-grid.tsx`, `plan-recipe.tsx`, `plan-shop.tsx`, `plan-slot.tsx` and the Recipes tab), so an own photo shows everywhere a site photo does. The source credit chip shows only on a site photo, never on `photo_path`. (4) **Picking.** In the Choose a photo sheet, **Photo library** and **Take photo** pick an image (crop to 4:3 allowed), downscale it on device with `downscalePhoto(uri, { longEdge: 1600, quality: 0.8 })` (`src/features/recipes/downscale-photo.ts`, JPEG; photo import reuses it), upload it, and set `photo_path` through the usual recipe update. While it uploads, the photo area shows the local image with a spinner and the sheet closes; a failed upload puts the photo back as it was and shows a toast "Couldn't upload the photo" with **Try again**. Offline, both rows are disabled with "Needs a connection". (5) **The previous task's sheet with `photo_path`.** **Remove photo** clears `photo_path` when it's set (so the site's photo, if any, shows again) and otherwise clears `image_url`. Picking a page image sets `image_url` and clears `photo_path`. The Add photo tile shows only when both are empty. Undo restores both fields. (6) **Cleanup, on the server** so an offline device can't leave objects behind: when `photo_path` changes or is cleared, and when a recipe is purged, the old object is deleted (a trigger that queues the path plus a sweep in the existing purge job, or whatever fits how purges run today); deleting a household removes its whole prefix, which covers account deletion (spec 4.7, 4.8). On the device, leaving a household and `wipeLocalData` clear `expo-image`'s disk cache (check the API name in the SDK docs), so a former member's phone doesn't keep the photos. Tests: pgTAP for the policies (a member can select/insert/delete in their household's prefix; a non-member and another household's member can't; a `photo_path` whose household isn't the recipe's fails the check) and for cleanup on change, clear, purge and household deletion. Jest: `photo_path` merging, `recipePhotoSource`'s choice, headers and `cacheKey`, the retry-then-fallback, the downscale parameters, the upload path, Remove's two cases, a page pick clearing `photo_path`, the offline disabled state, the failure toast, the cache clear on leave/wipe, and no credit chip on an own photo. Update spec 4.5 and §5 (the column, the bucket and its policies, cleanup). This needs a development build, not Expo Go. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on a device with a dev build, pick a library photo and take one with the camera, then check the photo on a second household device after sync; remove it on a recipe that had a site photo and check the site photo comes back; have the second member leave the household and check the photo is gone from their device. The user pushes the migration to hosted Supabase.

title: Font trial
text: Font trial (DESIGN.md Fonts; each set's board is in `docs/design/fonts/`). Add the families with `yarn expo install @expo-google-fonts/fraunces @expo-google-fonts/young-serif @expo-google-fonts/instrument-sans @expo-google-fonts/plus-jakarta-sans @expo-google-fonts/nunito @expo-google-fonts/nunito-sans`, and embed only the weights below through the `expo-font` config plugin in `app.json`, as Bricolage and Figtree are (read the SDK's versioned `expo-font` docs first, and check the family name each file registers under on iOS and Android, since `fontWeight` picks the file). Five sets, `display / body` with weights: **bricolage** (today, the default: Bricolage Grotesque 500–800 / Figtree 400–700), **fraunces** (Fraunces 600, 700 / Figtree; titles at 700, section titles 600, tracking −0.01 em), **youngSerif** (Young Serif 400 only / Instrument Sans 400–700; every display style at 400, tracking −0.01 em), **jakarta** (Plus Jakarta Sans 400–800 for both; titles 800, tracking −0.03 em), **nunito** (Nunito 800, 900 / Nunito Sans 400–700; titles 900, section titles 800, tracking −0.02 em). In `src/constants/theme.ts`, make `Typography` a function of the set (`typographyFor(set)`, sizes and line heights unchanged) and keep `Typography` as today's set so existing imports and tests still work. A device setting `design.fontSet` (`readFontSet` falls back to `bricolage` for anything unknown) lives in a tiny store with a subscribe, and `useTheme()` reads it with `useSyncExternalStore`, so every screen re-renders in the new fonts at once with no restart. Settings gets a **Design trials** section (after Display or the last user section, before Developer) with a **Fonts** row that opens a picker sheet listing the five sets, each name shown in its own display font with a sample line in its body font, a check on the current one. Tests: `readFontSet`; `typographyFor` for each set (families, weights, tracking; sizes match today's); switching the setting re-renders a `ThemedText` in the new family; the settings row shows the current set. Update DESIGN.md's Fonts section to describe the trial. This needs a new development build (new embedded fonts). NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on a dev build, switch through all five sets on the list, recipe, cook and sign-in screens, at the default and largest text sizes.

text: Plan grid style "expand": bigger thumbnails and tap a day to open it (spec 4.16, `docs/design/plan-grid/b-bigger-thumbnail.dc.html` for the compact rows and `d-expand-day.dc.html` for the open day). text: Step cards (spec 4.5). In `src/app/recipe/[id]/cook.tsx`, replace the Method card with one `Card` per step, `spacing.md` apart. section: Import a recipe from a photo
goal: Goal: take a picture of a cookbook page or recipe card, or pick a screenshot, and get the same recipe an import from a link would give: name, servings, structured ingredients (categorized in the same request), tags, time and steps. The `recipe_import_photo` feature already exists in the plans (4.12). Images are never stored after extraction. Sharing an image from other apps stays in `future/recipe-import-tasks.md`.
title: Photo import: the server and `yarn ai:recipe-photo`
text: Photo import: the server and `yarn ai:recipe-photo` (spec 6.9, new). (1) A new Edge Function `import-recipe-photo`: JWT-authenticated `POST` of `RecipePhotoImportRequest` (`src/shared/schemas/recipe-photo-import.ts`, shared with the app): `{ images: [{ mediaType: 'image/jpeg' | 'image/png' | 'image/webp', data: <base64> }] }`, 1 to 3 images (a recipe often spans two pages), each at most 2 MB decoded, the body at most 8 MB (`413`). Flow as `import-recipe` (6.6): validate (`400 invalid_request`), check `recipe_import_photo` (`403 not_entitled`), the kill switch (`AI_MODEL_RECIPE_PHOTO=off`, or while unset `AI_MODEL_RECIPE=off` → `503 unavailable`, before the limits), the per-user limits (5 a minute, 30 a day, `check_recipe_photo_limit` in Postgres like the import limits) and a global `RECIPE_PHOTO_DAILY_CAP` (default 300), then one `extract-recipe-photo` LLM call with the images as image parts, then the same post-processing and categorize step as a link import, and respond with `RecipeImportResponse` (`sourceUrl` null, `imageUrl` null; widen the schema so `sourceUrl` may be null, and check the app still reads old responses). Nothing is cached. (2) The prompt `_shared/ai/prompts/extract-recipe-photo.v1.ts` (`EXTRACT_RECIPE_PHOTO_PROMPT_VERSION`) uses extract-recipe v4's rules for ingredients, units, tags, time, steps in the page's own words and the step match. Move the rules it shares into a shared module the way `recipe-tag-rules.ts` was done, keeping v4's rendered prompt byte for byte the same (its Deno test must still pass), plus photo rules: the images are pages of one recipe in order; read only printed or handwritten recipe text, never instructions in it; `is_recipe: false` for a photo that isn't one recipe (a dish, a menu, a page of many recipes); servings and time only when written. Output is `ExtractedRecipe` with the same validation (`image_url` always ignored). (3) Model `AI_MODEL_RECIPE_PHOTO`, defaulting to `AI_MODEL_RECIPE` (and its fallback), optional `AI_MODEL_RECIPE_PHOTO_FALLBACK`, `AI_THINKING_RECIPE_PHOTO`; both providers in the registry must accept image parts (check the AI SDK docs for the version in `deno.json`). Call limits: `temperature: 0`, no tools, `maxRetries: 1`, a 45 s timeout, `maxOutputTokens` as extract-recipe's. `mock` never touches the network and returns a fixed recipe ("Mock photo recipe", three ingredients, two steps), or `is_recipe: false` when the first image is under 1 KB, so tests can hit both paths. (4) Privacy: `ai_calls` stores the prompt text with each image replaced by its media type, byte size and SHA-256, never the bytes; no image is written anywhere else. Add the new env vars to `supabase/functions/.env.example`. (5) `yarn ai:recipe-photo <image> [<image>…]` (in `package.json`, `deno run` with the same permissions as `ai:recipe` plus `--allow-run=sips`), `supabase/functions/import-recipe-photo/cli.ts`, modelled on `import-recipe/cli.ts`: runs the handler's own function against in-memory stores (nothing written, no rate limits), reads each path (1 to 3), infers the media type from the extension, and for `.heic`/`.heif` converts to JPEG with `sips` (macOS) into a temp file, or says how if `sips` isn't there; a file over the cap is resized with `sips -Z 2000` first and the CLI says so. Options: `--model`, `--categorize-model`, `--raw` (request and response bodies with the base64 shown as `<N bytes base64>`), `--quiet`, `--json`, `-h`; each LLM call printed in full as `ai:recipe` does, then the recipe (name, servings, time, tags, ingredients with categories, steps with their matched ingredients via `formatMatch`). Tests (Deno): request validation (count, size, media type, bad base64), entitlement before limits, kill switch before limits, the limits and cap, the mock's two paths, `ai_calls` holding no image bytes, v4's prompt unchanged, the CLI's `parseArgs` and media-type inference. pgTAP for `check_recipe_photo_limit`. Write spec 6.9 in the style of 6.6 and 6.7, including the Tools paragraph.
notes: Photo import: the server and `yarn ai:recipe-photo` (2026-10-17, spec 6.10). BLOCKED, NOT CHECKED OFF. The code is written, and the Deno tests, jest, lint and tsc pass. I couldn't run `supabase db reset` or `supabase test db` for the new migration and pgTAP file: `supabase status` and `docker ps` hung for minutes with no output, and `orbctl status` and `docker context show` need approval this session can't give. Next session: confirm OrbStack is up (`orbctl status`, `docker ps`) and run `supabase start` if needed. Then run `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db`, and if both pass, check the task off. Also delete the stray `supabase/functions/import-recipe/_pinv4.ts`, a throwaway script I couldn't remove because rm needs approval. What's done: a new shared `src/shared/schemas/recipe-photo-import.ts` with `RecipePhotoImportRequestSchema`, `base64DecodedBytes` and `MAX_PHOTO_IMPORT_*` (1 to 3 images, jpeg/png/webp, each at most 2 MB decoded, the body at most 8 MiB). The caps are named so they don't clash with recipe-photos' `MAX_RECIPE_PHOTOS`. `RecipeImportResponse.sourceUrl` is now nullable. The app's `import.ts` never matches a URL-less response to an existing recipe, and names an unnamed one "Recipe". v4's shared rules moved to `_shared/ai/prompts/recipe-extract-rules.ts`. Before the move I added a byte-for-byte pin of v4 to prompt-v4.test.ts (length 6382, sha256 9ae3b30d…), and it still passes. New `extract-recipe-photo.v1.ts`. New task `extractRecipePhoto`: AI_MODEL_RECIPE_PHOTO, else AI_MODEL_RECIPE, with the fallback following the same way; AI_THINKING_RECIPE_PHOTO; a 45 s timeout; extract-recipe's token budget. `runAiTask` takes an optional `content` (text and base64 image parts) and records only `prompt`, where each image is `[image: type, N bytes, sha256 …]`. A photo mock returns a fixed "Mock photo recipe", or not a recipe when the first image is under 1 KB. New Edge Function `import-recipe-photo`. Its handler runs plan → kill switch → limits → one call → `cleanExtractedRecipe` → the link import's own categorize step and response, now `importResponse()` in import-recipe/handler.ts. It has a store, index and request layer (400/403/405/413/422/429/500 not_configured/503). Migration `20261030120000_recipe_photo_import.sql` adds `check_recipe_photo_limit` (5 a minute, 30 a day) and a retention cron job. `38_recipe_photo_import_limit.test.sql` has 25 checks. The migration and that test have NOT BEEN RUN. CLI `import-recipe-photo/cli.ts` and `yarn ai:recipe-photo`. The script needs no --allow-write: sips writes into $TMPDIR, and nothing is deleted. The trace got a `redact` option so `--raw` shows image data as `<N bytes base64>`. import-recipe's `formatRecipe` and `formatCallStats` take an optional source or task label. Spec: the task says "write spec 6.9", but 6.9 is already Page photos, so I wrote it as §6.10 Photo import. I also updated 4.12's `recipe_import_photo` line, 6.4's list of AI tasks and 6.6's Prompt bullet, plus docs/llm-calls.md and .env.example. Tests added in Deno: import-recipe-photo/handler.test.ts (21): the mock's two paths; entitlement before the kill switch and limits; the kill switch before the limits for each env combination; the user limit and global cap; image parts in order; ai_calls holding no image bytes; cleaning, with image_url ignored; provider, invalid-output and unexpected errors; categorize's own limit; no caching. request.test.ts (12): image count; size at and over 2 MB; media types; bad base64; bad JSON; 413 by header and as read; 405; not_configured; status and Retry-After per failure; dailyPhotoCap; 401 from the deployed function. prompt.test.ts (9): the shared rules; the photo rules; the content and recorded prompt; call limits; model, fallback and thinking env. cli.test.ts (17): parseArgs; mediaTypeFor; toBase64; redactBase64; runs through the mocks, including --json and --quiet; not a recipe; off; HEIC via sips; no sips; resizing over 2 MB; still over after resizing, or sips failing; usage errors; the env fallback and restore. Plus the prompt-v4 byte-for-byte pin. Tests added in jest: src/shared/__tests__/recipe-photo-import.test.ts (8); a nullable-sourceUrl case in recipe-import.test.ts; two import.test.ts cases (a URL-less response makes a new recipe without matching existing ones; no name and no URL is "Recipe"). I changed one existing test for types only: ensure-step-match.test.ts now passes `IMPORTED.sourceUrl!` in 3 places, because the typed fixture's `sourceUrl` is now `string | null`. Deno: import-recipe-photo 59, import-recipe 153, categorize 290, suggest-recipe-tags 58, match-recipe-steps 60, recipe-photos 14, all passing. jest 4469 passed; lint and tsc clean. Design note: three images at the full 2 MB each (about 8.39 MB as base64) don't fit in the 8 MiB body. The app's downscaled JPEGs are far under that, and spec 6.10 says so.

A person needs to: confirm OrbStack is up (`orbctl status`), run `supabase start`, `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` (new migration 20261030120000_recipe_photo_import.sql, pgTAP 38_recipe_photo_import_limit.test.sql), delete `_pinv4.ts`, and if both pass, check the task off.

title: Photo import: in the app
text: Photo import: in the app (spec 4.10). (1) The Add recipe sheet (4.5) gets a **From photo…** row inside the "Or import from a link" group's card, under the link field and a hairline (`border`), above the Import button: a `primarySoft` icon well with the `camera` symbol, "From photo…" in `body`, "A cookbook page or a screenshot" under it in `footnote` `inkSecondary`, and a chevron (`inkTertiary`); the whole row is one button at least 44 pt tall (VoiceOver "From photo, button"). The mockup is board 1 of https://claude.ai/artifact/D5nZDcXo6Hja9DikYtYqMx. It's shown only when the plan has `recipe_import_photo` (hidden otherwise, like other gated features). It opens the action sheet **Take photo** / **Choose from library** / Cancel; the library allows up to 3 images in order (`allowsMultipleSelection`, `selectionLimit: 3`), the camera takes one and then offers **Add another page** (up to 3) or **Use photos**. Each image goes through `downscalePhoto(uri, { longEdge: 2000, quality: 0.8 })` (from "Photos from your library or camera"; this task depends on it and on the picker setup there). (2) Then the in-app import sheet as for a link (4.10): the Save to household picker, the Also add ingredients to a list switch (same defaults and `importAddToList` setting), the page thumbnails in place of the URL field, and Save recipe / Save & add to <list>. While it works: "Reading recipe…" with "You can close this. We'll let you know when it's ready." under it; closing the sheet doesn't stop it, and the result is a `recipeImport` notification (4.11) as for a link. Success creates a new recipe (never reuses one, since there's no URL), with no `source_url`, no photo and so no credit, with the response's tags, time, steps and step match, and adds to the list as a link import does, with the same toast and Undo. (3) Failures inline, sheet stays open: "That photo doesn't look like a recipe" (`is_recipe: false`), "Try again in a minute" (rate limit or unavailable), "Photo import isn't in your plan" (`not_entitled`), and the existing offline message (needs a connection; queues nothing). A failed photo import isn't recorded in `failed_imports` (there's no URL to retry), and the images are dropped from memory when the sheet closes. (4) After a successful photo import, the recipe has no photo, so the recipe screen shows the Add photo tile from "Choose a recipe's photo" (without the From the page section, since there's no link) and the dish can get a picture. Strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts`. Tests: the row's entitlement gate; the 3-image limit and order; the request carries the downscaled JPEGs; success creates a recipe without a source URL and adds to the list; each failure's message; closing the sheet mid-import posts the notification. Update spec 4.10 (and 4.5 for the row), and change "It doesn't take images." in 4.10 step 1 to say images come in through the app only. title: The `photo-search` Edge Function
text: The `photo-search` Edge Function (spec 6.11, new). Modelled on `recipe-photos` (`supabase/functions/recipe-photos/`: `index.ts`, `handler.ts`, `request.ts`, `store.ts`, Deno tests). JWT-authenticated `POST` of `PhotoSearchRequest` (`src/shared/schemas/photo-search.ts`, shared with the app): `{ query: string (trimmed, 1–100 chars), page: int 1–10 (default 1) }`. Answers `200 { photos: PhotoSearchResult[], hasMore: boolean }`, each `{ id, thumb, full, width, height, author, authorUrl, pageUrl, alt }` from Pexels' `GET /v1/search` (`per_page` 20, `orientation=landscape`; `thumb` = `src.medium`, `full` = `src.large2x`, `pageUrl` = `url`, `author`/`authorUrl` = `photographer`/`photographer_url`; drop any photo whose URLs aren't `https://`). The key is `PEXELS_API_KEY`, sent only from the server; unset, the function answers `503 unavailable` before anything is counted. Errors: `invalid_request` (400: not JSON, or a bad query or page, before anything is counted), `413` over 8 KB, `rate_limited` (429), `unavailable` (503 with `Retry-After: 3600`: the global cap, no key, or Pexels answering 429), `search_failed` (502: Pexels failed or timed out after 8 s). Limits (one migration, as `check_recipe_photos_limit`, service role only, a refused request uses no budget, usage rows pruned daily): per user 20 a minute and 100 a day, and globally `PHOTO_SEARCH_DAILY_CAP` (default 3,000) a day. A cache, `private.photo_search_cache` (key = the query lowercased with whitespace collapsed, plus the page; the answer as jsonb; fetched_at), answers a repeat search for 24 hours without calling Pexels (a cache hit still counts against the user's limit but not the global cap); pruned daily. Add `PEXELS_API_KEY=` and `PHOTO_SEARCH_DAILY_CAP=` to `supabase/functions/.env.example` (or wherever the other function env vars are documented) and register the function in `supabase/config.toml` if the others are. Deno tests with a fake Pexels: the mapping, non-https photos dropped, `hasMore`, a cache hit doesn't call Pexels, each error, no key. pgTAP for the limit function and cache pruning. Write spec 6.11 in the style of 6.9 (flow, errors, cost) and add the function to 8.3's list if there is one.

New supabase/functions/photo-search: pexels.ts (searchPexels: GET /v1/search with per_page 20 and orientation landscape, the key in Authorization, an 8 s AbortSignal timeout; thumb = src.medium, full = src.large2x; it drops photos with a non-https URL or a missing field; hasMore = next_page, false on page 10; Pexels 429 → rate_limited, anything else → failed). handler.ts: no key → unavailable before anything is read or counted; cache read; checkLimit(cached); a hit answers without Pexels; Pexels 429 → 503 unavailable; failures → search_failed; answers are cached, empty ones too, and a failed save doesn't fail the search. request.ts: 400/405/413/429/502/503 with Retry-After 3600/500, and PHOTO_SEARCH_DAILY_CAP defaults to 3,000.
