section: One tap out closes the add bar
goal: Goal: the two-step tap-out on a list's add bar (first tap drops the keyboard, second hides the bar and keeps the text) feels like a stuck bar. Make it one step: the first tap outside the field hides the keyboard and the bar together and throws the typed text away, the same as losing focus with the field empty does today.
title: One tap out closes the add bar and clears it
text: One tap out closes the add bar and clears it (spec 4.1, 4.2). In `src/features/lists/list-screen.tsx`, while the add field is focused with text in it, a tap outside the bar (the list's empty space below or between the rows, the header, the compact title) now hides the keyboard and the bar at once and clears `addText` (and its chips), so + (and `openAdd`) next opens an empty, focused bar. A tap on a row, chip or control does what it does now. With the field empty, losing focus still hides the bar at once, as now. Select mode still swaps the bar out and clears the text, as now. Submitting from the keyboard still adds and keeps the bar open, as now. The second-tap machinery goes: `addTucked`, `tapOutHidesBar` and the `onStartShouldSetResponder` that uses it, and `showAddBar` no longer stays up just because `addText !== ''`; update the comments above them. Jest (`src/features/lists/__tests__/list-screen.test.tsx`): type text, tap out once, the bar is gone; + brings it back empty and focused; with an empty field, blur hides it straight away; replace the tests for the old two-step behavior. Update spec 4.1 (the tab bar's + bullet) and 4.2 (Add mode) where they describe the first tap out keeping the bar and its text and a second tap out hiding it.
notes: One tap out closes the add bar and clears it (2026-10-18, spec 4.1, 4.2): DONE, checked off. In `list-screen.tsx`, `addTucked`, `tapOutHidesBar` and the viewport's `onStartShouldSetResponder`/`onResponderRelease` are gone. `showAddBar` is now `!selection && (addOpen || adding)`, and `addFocusChange(false)` clears `addText`, so the first tap out (the keyboard going) hides the bar, which unmounts and takes its text and chips with it. + then opens it empty and focused. Submit keeps focus (`submitBehavior="submit"`), so the bar stays open after an add. Comments updated, and so is `ItemAddBar`'s `initialText` doc, which only the recipe screen still uses that way. Spec 4.1 and 4.2 are rewritten for one tap out. Spec 4.5's recipe-screen add bar keeps its two-step behaviour (out of scope), so I changed its "hides as a list's add bar does (4.1)" to say it hides in two steps, unlike a list's. Tests: in `list-screen.test.tsx` the old "it goes again… stays while something is" test and the "a second tap out" describe (old behaviour) are replaced by a "one tap out" describe with 10 cases: the first tap out with text hides the bar (this would have failed before), the viewport no longer takes taps, + brings it back empty and focused, the thrown-away text no longer marks rows "already on list", a reopened bar closes on the next tap out, an empty field hides at once, a field cleared before the tap out, a row tap keeps the bar and its text, submit keeps the bar open, and Select mode still swaps it out and clears it. jest 5026 passed / 2 skipped, lint and tsc are clean. title: Show a one-time "Hold + for more ways to add" hint over the tab bar's +
text: Show a one-time "Hold + for more ways to add" hint over the tab bar's + (spec 4.1, "The + hint"). In `src/features/tabs/add-button.ts`, `pressAddButton` increments the device setting `tabBar.addTapCount` (capped at 3) through `getDeviceSetting` / `setDeviceSetting` (`src/features/settings/device-settings.ts`). Opening the long-press menu, or using its VoiceOver action "More ways to add" (`src/features/tabs/add-menu.ts`), sets `tabBar.addHintSeen` to true. Put the decision in one pure function beside them, `shouldShowAddHint({ tapCount, seen, screenReaderOn, sheetOpen, selecting })`, and keep the threshold (3) and the timeout (8 s) as named constants there. The list screen (`src/features/lists/list-screen.tsx`), when add mode ends (the add field blurs and the bar hides), checks it. With VoiceOver on (`AccessibilityInfo.isScreenReaderEnabled`), it marks the hint seen and shows nothing. Otherwise it shows the callout anchored above + in the custom tab bar (`src/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`): a `surface` card with a caret, `footnote` text, the floating shadow, fade in/out, `pointerEvents` so a tap anywhere dismisses it and still goes through. Any dismissal (tap, long-press on +, 8 s) sets `tabBar.addHintSeen`. It shows at most once. Strings: `tabs.addHint` in `en.ts` / `es.ts` ("Hold + for more ways to add" / "Mantén presionado + para más formas de agregar"). In Settings > Developer (`src/app/(tabs)/settings/developer.tsx`), add a row **Show the + hint again** that clears `tabBar.addHintSeen` and sets `tabBar.addTapCount` to 3, with a toast "The + hint will show after your next add". Jest: `shouldShowAddHint` truth table (under 3 taps, seen, VoiceOver, sheet open, Select mode); tapping + three times then blurring the add field shows the hint; a long-press before that means it never shows; dismissing sets the flag, so the next blur doesn't show it again; the Developer row resets it. The spec bullet is already in place; if what you build differs from it, update it. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on a simulator, Developer > Show the + hint again, add an item, tap out: the callout points at +, fades after 8 s; repeat and long-press + while it shows: the menu opens and the callout goes.

Add `supabase/functions/_shared/ai/prompts/extract-recipe.v5.ts` (keep v4's file, bump the version so the cache key changes): the JSON-LD steps go to the model with unnumbered `## <name>` heading lines between the numbered steps, the step match still numbers step strings only, and the output adds `choice_sections` (1-based heading numbers, as spec 6.6 says: only alternatives, never a section the others build on, never just one); without JSON-LD, the model's `steps` may include `## <name>` lines where the page names sections. Put the section rules in `recipe-extract-rules.ts` so photo import shares them, and add `extract-recipe-photo.v2.ts` the same way. The server turns `## ` lines into heading entries, sets `choice: true` from `choice_sections` (out-of-range or single numbers ignored), and runs `cleanRecipeSteps`. Save the familystylefood.com chicken-thigh-marinade page as `supabase/functions/import-recipe/eval/fixtures/jsonld-familystylefood-chicken-thigh-marinade.html` (add it to `SOURCES.md` and `expected.json`: 5 sections, the last 4 a choice group). Jest / Deno tests: `findRecipe` on that fixture gives "Marinate the chicken", then "Grilling", "Baking", "Pan-Frying", "Broiling" headings around the right steps; the existing JSON-LD fixtures' steps are unchanged (none of them has named sections, or update their expectations if one does); a model answer with `choice_sections: [2,3,4,5]` sets `choice` on those four only; `[1]` and `[9]` set nothing; `## ` lines in page-text steps become headings. Run `yarn ai:eval:recipe` with the mock and note the real-model result in progress.md (NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK if no key: `yarn ai:recipe https://familystylefood.com/chicken-thigh-marinade/` shows the four methods as one choice group).
notes: Imports keep JSON-LD sections and mark the alternatives (2026-10-18, spec 6.6, 6.10): BLOCKED, left unchecked, no code changed. Checks: `yarn jest` (189 suites pass; one run had a load-flaky failure in `src/features/auth/__tests__/account.test.ts`, which passes alone and on the next two full runs, unrelated to this change), `yarn expo lint`, `yarn tsc --noEmit`, the Deno suites for import-recipe (175), import-recipe-photo, categorize-ingredients, match-recipe-steps, suggest-recipe-tags, generate-recipe-photo and recipe-photos, and `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1321 pass). `yarn ai:eval:recipe --model mock`: sections 1/2 (the mock never marks a choice, as expected). title: The Method card and the Steps sheet show and edit sections
text: The Method card and the Steps sheet show and edit sections (spec 4.5 "Step sections": Method card, Steps sheet; boards A and D). `src/features/recipes/recipe-method-card.tsx`: section titles over their steps, and a choice group after a hairline with its label ("Then cook it one way" / "Cook it one way", "4 ways"), the option pills and the picked option's steps; numbering, the header count and the recipe screen's "Method · N" switch label follow `stepPath` for the card's pick (first option on each visit; screen state, not saved). VoiceOver: titles are headers, the pills a radio group. `src/app/recipe/[id]/steps.tsx` and `stepsToText` / `stepsFromText` (`recipe-view.ts`): headings round-trip as `# <name>` lines; the label reads "One step per line · # starts a section"; with two or more headings in the text, the **Choose one when cooking** card lists them live with a checkbox each and the footnote, ticks kept by heading text; Save writes headings with `choice` from the ticks (then `ensureStepMatch` as now). Strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts` as the spec gives them. Tokens from DESIGN.md only. Jest: a sectioned recipe renders its titles; tapping a pill swaps the steps and renumbers them, and the count follows; a recipe without headings renders exactly as before; the sheet turns `# Grill` into a heading, drops an empty `#`, shows the choice card only from two headings, and saves ticked headings with `choice: true`; text → entries → text round-trips.
notes: The Method card and the Steps sheet show and edit sections (2026-10-18, spec 4.5 "Step sections", boards A and D): DONE, checked off. `recipe-view.ts`: `stepsToText` writes headings as `# <name>`; `stepsFromText(text, choices)` turns `#` lines into headings (#s and following spaces dropped, empty dropped, 80-char cap, past the 20th dropped), `choice: true` when the name is in `choices`, still null without a step string; new `stepHeadingsInText`, `choiceHeadings`, and the pure `methodBlocks(entries, picks)` / `withPick`. `RecipeMethodCard` renders section titles (`sectionLabel` `inkSecondary`, VoiceOver headers), a choice group after a hairline with "Then cook it one way" / "Cook it one way" and "N ways", the options as a radiogroup of new `Pill muted primary` pills (`pillLook` `muted`: `surfaceMuted`/`ink` off), then the picked option's steps numbered along the path; the header count follows. The recipe screen holds the picks (first option every visit) so "Method · N" counts `stepPath`. Steps sheet: new label, and with ≥2 headings the Choose one when cooking card (checkbox rows, ticks keyed by heading text) and footnote; Save writes `stepsFromText(text, choices)` then `ensureStepMatch`. en/es strings; DESIGN.md Method card and Steps sheet entries updated. Tests: `recipe-method.test.tsx` replaced the "before they are shown" block (that behavior changed on purpose) with "the Method card with step sections" (8 tests: titles as headers, radiogroup and colours, tapping Bake/Pan-fry renumbers and the header and switch counts follow, pick resets per visit, group-first label, lone choice reads ordinary, no headings unchanged, heading-only empty state) and "the Steps sheet with step sections" (5: `#` lines and ticks, card only from two headings and live, Save with ticked choices, renaming drops a tick, untouched save is lossless); the existing sheet test's label assertion changed to the new string. `recipe-view.test.ts`: 9 heading-parsing/round-trip tests and 4 `methodBlocks`/`withPick` tests. `appearance.test.ts`: muted pill look and contrast. No real AI calls.

title: Cook mode asks which method you're using
text: Cook mode asks which method you're using (spec 4.5 "Step sections": Cook mode; boards B and C). In `src/app/recipe/[id]/cook.tsx` and `src/features/recipes/cook-match.ts`: steps in their sections under their titles; a choice group shows the **How are you cooking it?** card (current when every step before it is ticked, upcoming otherwise; one row per option with its step count); picking replaces it with that section, titled, with **Change method** bringing the card back and the option's ticks kept; numbering follows `stepPath`; the top bar counts the shared steps plus the picked options' and reads "3 steps done · pick a method" while a group has no pick; a named section that's all ticked and behind the current card folds to one row ("Marinate the chicken · 3 done") that unfolds on tap. Picks and folds are screen state, like ticks. Mark step done after the last step before a group scrolls the picker into view (instantly under Reduce Motion). section: One field on the Add recipe sheet
goal: Goal: the Add recipe sheet has a name field with Create, then "Or import from a link" heading a URL field *and* the From photo… row, with Import under the photo row, so it reads as though Import imports the photo, and two big buttons compete. The name field already imports a link typed into it (`nameAction`, `src/features/recipes/add-recipe.ts`), so the separate link field is redundant. Make it one field and one button. title: One "Paste a link or type a name" field on the Add recipe sheet
text: One "Paste a link or type a name" field on the Add recipe sheet (spec 4.5 "Start from the recipe"; boards B1 and B2). In `src/app/add-recipe.tsx`: drop the "New recipe" section label, the whole "Or import from a link" group (its heading, the link field, its Paste button and the Import button) and the `link` state. What's left, under the sheet title: with `recipe_import`, a **Paste link** chip (`primarySoft` / `onPrimarySoft`, a `doc.on.clipboard` glyph, at least 44 pt tall) above the field, only while `Clipboard.hasUrlAsync()` is true; tapping it reads the clipboard (`urlFromText`), puts the link in the field and hides the chip. The one field (placeholder "Paste a link or type a name" with import, "Recipe name" without; VoiceOver label "Recipe name or link" / "Recipe name") always gets focus. While `nameAction` is `import`, a `link` glyph sits at the field's start and a `footnote` `inkSecondary` line under it reads "We'll bring in the ingredients, steps and photo." The one `PrimaryButton` stays as now: **Create**, or **Import recipe** with the `link` icon for a link, disabled while empty; Return does the same; without import a link still gets the "That's a link…" footnote and a disabled Create. With `recipe_import_photo`, an "or" divider (two `border` hairlines around `footnote` `inkTertiary` "or") and the **From photo…** row in a card of its own, unchanged otherwise (`FromPhotoRow` loses its top border). The `focus=link` param goes: remove it from the Recipes tab's `importFromLink` (`src/app/(tabs)/recipes/index.tsx`), which just opens the sheet. Update the component's doc comment. Tokens from DESIGN.md only. Jest (`src/features/recipes/__tests__/add-recipe-sheet.test.tsx`): one text field, no "Or import from a link", no Import button; typing a name and Create opens the new recipe; typing a link shows the note and **Import recipe**, which opens the import sheet with the normalized URL; the chip shows only when the clipboard has a URL and fills the field; without `recipe_import` there's no chip, the placeholder is "Recipe name" and a link is refused; the From photo row shows only with `recipe_import_photo`. title: The empty list gets a glyph, a headline and two actions
text: The empty list gets a glyph, a headline and two actions (spec 4.1; board C). Extend `EmptyState` (`src/components/empty-state.tsx`) with optional `icon` (an SF Symbol name), `title` and `actions`, leaving its current callers as they are: with them, a 72 pt `primarySoft` tile (radius `card`, add a `sizes.emptyIcon` token) holding the glyph in `onPrimarySoft`, 20 pt under it the title in `title` `ink` (centred, a VoiceOver header), 8 pt under that the message in `callout` `inkSecondary`, then 24 pt down the actions stacked and centred, 8 pt apart; the block sits about 40% down the space rather than dead centre, and still scrolls under large Dynamic Type. In `src/features/lists/list-screen.tsx`, the empty list's `ListEmptyComponent` uses it: `cart` glyph, title "Your list is empty", message "Add what you need, or pull in a recipe's ingredients in one go.", then a `Pill soft` **Add an item** with a `plus` glyph that calls `openAdd` (the same as the tab bar's +), and a plain `primary` `Button` **Add from a recipe** with a `fork.knife` glyph that opens the Recipes tab (`router.navigate('/recipes')`). Both at least 44 pt tall. While the list has no items, the view menu (`arrow.up.arrow.down`) is hidden, as the Recipes tab hides its sort button with no recipes; ⋯ stays. A list with only checked items isn't empty and is unchanged. Strings in `en.ts` / `es.ts` under `lists.screen`: `emptyTitle` ("Your list is empty" / "Tu lista está vacía"), `empty` reworded ("Add what you need, or pull in a recipe's ingredients in one go." / "Agrega lo que necesitas o trae los ingredientes de una receta de una vez."), `emptyAddItem` ("Add an item" / "Agregar un artículo"), `emptyAddFromRecipe` ("Add from a recipe" / "Agregar de una receta"). Tokens from DESIGN.md only; add an **Empty state** bullet to DESIGN.md's components describing the variant. Jest (`src/features/lists/__tests__/list-screen.test.tsx`): an empty list shows the title, message and both actions (update the test that expects the old line); **Add an item** opens the add bar focused; **Add from a recipe** navigates to `/recipes`; the view menu is absent on an empty list and back once an item is added; the other `EmptyState` callers render as before. Add the empty list to spec 4.1 (the list screen) with the copy above. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on a simulator, a new empty list shows board C in both light and dark; Add an item opens the bar; Add from a recipe lands on Recipes; add an item and the view menu comes back.

Changed two existing tests because the copy changed: "an empty list says so and offers the add bar" and "an empty list says so in Spanish". No real AI calls. goal: Goal: the app is run for one person, family and maybe a few strangers, not for revenue. New users should get every AI feature (it's part of what makes the app usable), each user's spending is bounded by their own daily limits, and there are no global daily caps (a cap across all users makes no sense if usage grows). Plans get names that are easy to remember: **none** (no AI), **basic** (categorize and step matching), **plus** (every feature, with per-user monthly limits; the new default) and **unlimited** (every feature, no monthly limits; for family). Each plan sets its own monthly limit per feature in a `plan_limits` table, so a paid plan with different limits can be added later by inserting rows, and a number can be changed in the Table Editor without a migration or deploy. Plus's limits are sized so one user maxing out every feature costs about $1 a month. Per-minute limits, the `off` kill switches and "one AI photo per recipe, ever" stay the same on every plan. If what you build differs from what these tasks say, update the spec to match.
title: Rename the plans and add unlimited; plus becomes the default
text: Rename the plans and add unlimited; plus becomes the default (spec 4.12, 5). New migration (don't edit `20261012200000_plans.sql`): plan ids are text primary keys and `user_plans.plan_id` references them without `on update cascade`, so insert the new plans `none` ("None", no features), `basic` ("Basic": `categorize`, `step_ingredients`) and `unlimited` ("Unlimited": every feature), move existing `user_plans` rows (`base` → `none`, `standard` → `basic`), put jgpasch@gmail.com on `unlimited` (as the plans migration put them on plus), clear `is_default` on `standard` and set it on `plus` (the partial unique index allows only one, so clear first), then delete `base` and `standard` (their `plan_features` cascade). `plus` keeps its id, name and features. It must run cleanly on hosted, where real users have rows. `supabase/seed.sql`: the dev user goes on `unlimited`. App: `src/features/plans/features.ts` assumes the default plan's features until the first load, so `DEFAULT_FEATURES` becomes plus's (all six; it's stale today, `['categorize']` while standard also has `step_ingredients`), and update the comments that say "standard". pgTAP (`supabase/tests/17_plans.test.sql`): the plans and their features are exactly the four above, `plus` is the one default, a user with no row gets plus's features, the every-plan-with-`recipe_import`-has-`categorize` check still passes, and replace the `base` / `standard` fixtures. Jest: the store before the first load has plus's features. Update spec 4.12 (the seeded plans, the default, the owner's plan, local dev's plan, the app's fallback), `docs/admin.md` ("Change a user's plan": the four ids and what each gets) and any other doc that names `base`, `standard` or the old default. In progress.md, give the hosted step: `supabase db push`.

title: Remove the global daily caps
text: Remove the global daily caps (spec 6.1, 6.6–6.11). Each per-user limit stays exactly as it is; only the across-all-users cap goes. SQL, in one new migration: `check_categorize_limit`, `check_recipe_import_limit`, `check_recipe_tags_limit`, `check_step_match_limit`, `check_recipe_photos_limit`, `check_recipe_photo_limit` and `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` lose their `p_daily_cap` argument and the `global_cap` answer (drop and recreate each with its new signature, with the same revokes and grants, and only `service_role` may execute it), and drop the `private.*_daily_total` tables they used (`categorize_daily_total`, `recipe_import_daily_total`, and the others; find them in the migrations), and reschedule each prune job without its `delete from private.*_daily_total` (each job also prunes that feature's usage table, which must keep being pruned). Edge Functions: in `categorize-ingredients`, `import-recipe`, `suggest-recipe-tags`, `match-recipe-steps`, `recipe-photos`, `import-recipe-photo` and `generate-recipe-photo`, remove the cap env vars (`CATEGORIZE_DAILY_NAME_CAP`, `RECIPE_IMPORT_DAILY_CAP`, `RECIPE_TAGS_DAILY_CAP`, `STEP_MATCH_DAILY_CAP`, `RECIPE_PHOTOS_DAILY_CAP`, `RECIPE_PHOTO_DAILY_CAP`, `RECIPE_PHOTO_AI_DAILY_CAP`), their `DEFAULT_*_CAP` constants and `parseCap` readers in each `request.ts`, the `global_cap` → 503 branches, and their tests; a 503 `unavailable` still comes from the kill switches and provider errors, with the same `Retry-After` as now. The app needs no change (it already treats 503 as "Try again in a minute" or the photo wording), but check that nothing in `src/` mentions a global cap. Remove the lines from `supabase/functions/.env.example`. pgTAP: update each limit function's test (per-user limits still refuse with `user_limit`, a refused request still uses no budget, nothing returns `global_cap`, and the old signatures are gone). Update spec 6.1–6.11's **Cost** / **Limits** paragraphs, flows and error lists (`unavailable` is the kill switch or a provider error only), section 5's description of the usage tables, and `docs/alpha-testing.md` (it tells you to set lower caps in `.env.production.local`). In progress.md, give the hosted steps for a person to run: `supabase db push`, deploy the seven functions (`supabase functions deploy <name>` for each), and `supabase secrets unset` for whichever of the seven cap names `supabase secrets list` shows (and delete them from `supabase/functions/.env.production.local`).
notes: Remove the global daily caps (2026-10-18, spec 6.1, 6.4, 6.6–6.11, 5): DONE, checked off. New migration `20261112120000_drop_global_caps.sql` drops and recreates `check_categorize_limit(user_id, new_names)`, `check_recipe_import_limit(user_id)`, `check_recipe_tags_limit(user_id)`, `check_step_match_limit(user_id)`, `check_recipe_photos_limit(user_id)`, `check_recipe_photo_limit(user_id)` and `reserve_recipe_photo_ai(user_id, recipe_id)` without `p_daily_cap` or the `global_cap` answer (per-user limits unchanged; same revokes, `service_role` only; a null user to categorize, the sweep, now just answers `ok`), drops the seven `private.*_daily_total` tables, reschedules the six usage retention jobs to prune only their usage tables, and unschedules `recipe-photo-ai-total-retention` (it pruned only the AI photo total). Edge Functions: the seven functions lose their cap env vars, `DEFAULT_*_CAP` constants, `daily*Cap` readers, `parseCap` (in categorize's request.ts) and the `global_cap` → 503 branches; `LimitResult` is `'ok' | 'user_limit'`; categorize now never answers 503, and recipe-photos lost its `unavailable` failure and `PAUSED_RETRY_AFTER` (it has no kill switch); the other 503s (kill switches, provider errors) keep their Retry-After. Deno tests: removed the global-cap and cap-reader tests; importRecipe's "throws ImportRecipeError" test now uses the per-user limit (`rate_limited`) since `global_cap` is gone; all seven suites pass (287, 173, 56, 58, 12, 60, 47). App: comments only (`suggest-tags.ts`, `recipe-photos.ts`, the generate-recipe-photo schema) and two test titles (`recipe-photos.test.ts`; `recipe-photo-sheet.test.tsx` "the cap (503)" → "a kill switch (503)"); nothing in `src/` mentions a global cap. pgTAP (07, 11, 20, 34, 36, 38, 46): calls use the new signatures; each global-cap section is replaced by "another user still passes whatever others used, and it counts against their own limits", `hasnt_function` for the old signature, `hasnt_table` for the daily total, and the retention job's command being exactly its usage-table delete (46: the AI photo total's job is gone); the negative-cap tests went (07 now checks a null user has no name limit; 46 that a null user is refused). `.env.example` lost the six cap lines (RECIPE_PHOTOS_DAILY_CAP was never in it). Spec 5 (usage counters, AI photos), 6.4, 6.6–6.11 updated (the §10 "Landed" history left as it was); `docs/alpha-testing.md`, `docs/setup.md` and the README no longer mention caps. `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1305) pass; jest, lint, tsc pass. No real AI calls. HOSTED STEPS (by hand): `supabase db push`, then right away deploy all seven (the old functions pass `p_daily_cap`, which the new SQL functions don't take): `supabase functions deploy categorize-ingredients`, `supabase functions deploy import-recipe`, `supabase functions deploy suggest-recipe-tags`, `supabase functions deploy match-recipe-steps`, `supabase functions deploy recipe-photos`, `supabase functions deploy import-recipe-photo`, `supabase functions deploy generate-recipe-photo`; then `supabase secrets list` and `supabase secrets unset` whichever of `CATEGORIZE_DAILY_NAME_CAP RECIPE_IMPORT_DAILY_CAP RECIPE_TAGS_DAILY_CAP STEP_MATCH_DAILY_CAP RECIPE_PHOTOS_DAILY_CAP RECIPE_PHOTO_DAILY_CAP RECIPE_PHOTO_AI_DAILY_CAP` it shows, and delete them from `supabase/functions/.env.production.local` (it has `CATEGORIZE_DAILY_NAME_CAP` and `RECIPE_IMPORT_DAILY_CAP`).

title: Monthly limits per plan in a `plan_limits` table, and a per-user limit on AI photos
text: Monthly limits per plan in a `plan_limits` table, and a per-user limit on AI photos (spec 4.12, 5, 6.1, 6.6–6.11). Today each `check_*_limit` function hard-codes a per-user daily limit, the same on every plan. Replace the daily limits with **monthly** ones (the calendar month in UTC, resetting on the 1st), set per plan in data. New migration: `public.plan_limits (plan_id text references public.plans on delete cascade, feature text, monthly_limit integer check (monthly_limit >= 0), primary key (plan_id, feature))`, `feature` checked against the same keys as `plan_features`, RLS on and every privilege revoked from `public`, `anon` and `authenticated` (only the dashboard and the `security definer` limit functions read it). A null `monthly_limit` means no monthly limit; so does a plan with a feature but no `plan_limits` row for it (say so in the table's comment, and in `docs/admin.md` that deleting a row lifts the limit). Seed: **plus** `categorize` 250 (LLM-bound names a month), `step_ingredients` 100, `recipe_import` 40, `recipe_import_photo` 20, `recipe_tags` 50, `recipe_photo_ai` 15; **basic** `categorize` 250, `step_ingredients` 100; **unlimited** a row per feature with `monthly_limit` null (explicit, so the Table Editor shows it); **none** no rows. **First month**: an account younger than 30 days (`auth.users.created_at`) gets twice its plan's limits, so importing a collection on day one doesn't hit the wall; keep the 30 days and the 2× as named constants in the one SQL function that resolves limits, with a comment. Add `private.monthly_limit(p_user_id uuid, p_feature text, p_household_id uuid default null) returns integer` that resolves the user's plan the same way `has_feature` does (their `user_plans` row, else the default plan; it ignores the household, like `has_feature`, so both can go per household together), applies the first-month doubling and returns the limit, or null. The usage tables keep counting per user and UTC day; each of `check_categorize_limit`, `check_recipe_import_limit`, `check_recipe_tags_limit`, `check_step_match_limit` and `check_recipe_photo_limit` sums the user's rows for the current month and compares that (categorize: the month's LLM-bound names plus `p_new_names`) with `private.monthly_limit` for its feature instead of the hard-coded daily number, skipping the check when it's null. They answer a new `monthly_limit` (distinct from `user_limit`, which is now only the per-minute limit), still before anything is written, so a refused request uses no budget. The per-minute limits stay hard-coded and apply on every plan (they catch a client stuck in a loop). Keep counting usage even with no limit, so the numbers stay visible. Change each prune job to keep usage rows for 40 days (they keep 30 or fewer today), so a month's sum is always complete. `check_recipe_photos_limit` (page photos, no LLM and no feature key) keeps its hard-coded 50 a day. **AI photos**: today the only limit on `generate-recipe-photo` is one photo per recipe, and a user can make any number of recipes. `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` gets a monthly limit from `private.monthly_limit(p_user_id, 'recipe_photo_ai')`, counted at the reservation in a new `private.recipe_photo_ai_usage` table (per user and UTC day, like the other usage tables, pruned the same way; a released slot isn't given back, since its calls were made), and answers `monthly_limit` once the user has reserved that many this month, checked after `not_found` and `already_generated` and before anything is written. One AI photo per recipe stays on every plan. **Edge Functions**: `monthly_limit` answers **429** with a new error code `limit_reached` and `resets_at` (the first instant of next month, UTC, ISO 8601) in the error body, in all six functions and their shared response schemas (`src/shared/schemas/`); `user_limit` stays `rate_limited`. The functions don't pass or know any limit number. **App**: `limit_reached` is never "Try again in a minute". Link import (`import.ts`, `import-sheet.ts`): "You've used this month's recipe imports. They reset on <date>." Photo import: "You've used this month's photo imports. They reset on <date>." Tag suggestions (`suggest-tags.ts`): "You've used this month's tag suggestions. They reset on <date>." AI photo: "You've used this month's AI photos. They reset on <date>." The date is `resets_at` as a short local date (e.g. "Nov 1"). Shares (`share-drain.ts`, `share-queue-status.ts`, `failed-imports.ts`): a share answered `limit_reached` keeps its file and stops the drain without counting an attempt, like a rate limit, and the imports card shows the import wording, so the shares import once the month resets. Background work stays silent: step matching (`ensure-step-match.ts`) stops for the session on `limit_reached` (like `not_entitled`); categorize leaves the names `pending`, and the catch-up keeps them for later (a refused request costs nothing). Strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts`. pgTAP: `plan_limits` holds exactly the seeded rows; `authenticated` can't read it; `private.monthly_limit` gives a user with no `user_plans` row plus's limits, a `basic` user basic's, an `unlimited` user null, null for a feature with no row, and twice the limit for an account 29 days old but not one 31 days old; for each limit function, a `plus` user is refused with `monthly_limit` once the month's rows (spread over several days) reach plus's number, a `basic` user at basic's, an `unlimited` user passes it but is still refused with `user_limit` by the per-minute limit, last month's usage doesn't count, and changing a `plan_limits` row changes the limit at once; the 16th AI photo reservation in a month is `monthly_limit` for an older plus account, the 1st of the next month is fine, and `not_found` / `already_generated` / `monthly_limit` write nothing. Deno tests, per function: `monthly_limit` answers 429 `limit_reached` with the next month's `resets_at` and makes no model call; `user_limit` still answers `rate_limited`. Jest: each wording above with its date; a share answered `limit_reached` stays queued without an attempt counted; step matching stops for the session. Update spec 4.12 (plans set monthly limits through `plan_limits`, the seeded numbers, the first-month doubling, what unlimited means: no monthly limits, per-minute limits and one AI photo per recipe kept), section 5 (`plan_limits`, `recipe_photo_ai_usage`, the usage tables kept 40 days), each **Cost** / **Limits** paragraph and error list in 6.1–6.11 (the monthly number comes from the user's plan; give plus's; `limit_reached`), 4.10's failure wordings, and `docs/admin.md` (change a limit by editing a `plan_limits` row; unlimited is the plan for family; a new plan needs its `plan_features` and `plan_limits` rows). In progress.md, give the hosted steps: `supabase db push` and deploy the six AI functions (`supabase functions deploy <name>` for each).
notes: Per-user rate limit (spec 6.4), done after the task was reworded to settle the earlier blocker. Migration `20261009230000_categorize_limit.sql`: `private.categorize_usage` (PK user_id+day, FK to auth.users on delete cascade) and `private.categorize_daily_total`, with RLS on and all grants revoked from public/anon/authenticated. `public.check_categorize_limit(p_user_id, p_new_names, p_daily_cap) returns text` is `security definer`, `search_path = ''`, and only service_role can execute it. Days are UTC and the minute is a fixed `date_trunc('minute')` window. It upserts a zero row, then locks the user row and then the day's total `for update`. Counters change only on 'ok'; a refused first request leaves a zero row. A negative or null argument raises 22023. A cron job (`categorize-usage-retention`) deletes old rows. Edge Function: `CategorizeStore.checkLimit(newNames)` calls the RPC. `categorize` calls it once per request, after reading the DB and before writing anything, with the LLM-bound count (0 when AI is off). On a refusal it throws `CategorizeLimitError(reason)`, so a refused request writes no pending rows. `handleRequest` maps `user_limit` to 429 `rate_limited` and `global_cap` to 503 `daily_cap_reached` with `Retry-After: 3600`. `index.ts` builds the store with the user id and `dailyNameCap(CATEGORIZE_DAILY_NAME_CAP)` (default 20,000; invalid values fall back to it). Documented in `supabase/functions/.env.example`. Tests: new pgTAP `07_categorize_limit.test.sql` (35): 60 a minute, then refused even with 0 names; another user unaffected; the window resets; 500/501 names a day, and a batch that crosses the limit is refused whole; refused requests leave counters unchanged; the global cap refuses every user, but 0 new names still gets ok; a null user skips the per-user limits but not the cap and writes no usage row; bad args raise; anon/authenticated can't call the function or read the tables, and service_role can call it. Deno, 10 new (76 pass): checkLimit counts only LLM-bound names; all-known counts 0; off counts 0; user_limit/global_cap refuse with no LLM call and no writes; a check error propagates; 429; 503 + Retry-After; 400 comes before the limit; `dailyNameCap` parsing. The existing FakeStore got a `checkLimit` method; no existing assertions changed. jest (426), lint, tsc, `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` (132) pass. Not checked by hand against the served function: the RPC call in `store.ts` has no automated test.

Monthly limits per plan in `plan_limits`, and a monthly limit on AI photos (2026-10-18, spec 4.12, 5, 6.1, 6.6–6.11): DONE, checked off. Iteration 2 (commit 62eacaa) wrote the code and tests but stopped before the docs and before checking the task off, with no progress entry. This session checked that work against the task and finished it. Already in place from iteration 2: migration `20261113120000_plan_limits.sql` (`public.plan_limits` with the seed, RLS on and no client privileges; `private.recipe_photo_ai_usage`; `private.monthly_limit` with the 30-day / 2× first-month constants; `private.monthly_usage`; the five `check_*_limit` functions and `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` answering `monthly_limit` before any write; every usage table kept 40 days, plus a 03:49 retention job for AI photo usage; `check_recipe_photos_limit` unchanged at 50 a day). Edge Functions: `_shared/limits.ts` (`monthlyResetsAt`, `limitReachedResponse`) gives 429 `limit_reached` + `resets_at` in all six functions; `user_limit` stays `rate_limited`. App: `src/features/plans/limits.ts` (`limitResetsAt`, `resetDate`: a short date read in UTC so it's always the 1st, e.g. "Nov 1"), the link, photo, tag and AI photo wordings in en/es, shares keep their file without counting an attempt, the imports card and failed-imports rows use the import wording, step matching stops for the session, categorize leaves names pending. goal: Goal: a small web app, run locally against hosted Supabase, for the jobs the dashboard makes awkward: find a user and change their plan, edit what each plan includes and its monthly limits, and see how much of each AI feature people use. It lives in `admin/` in this repo. The dashboard and the `admin.*` SQL snippets stay for everything else (deleting a user, reading logs). ### Decisions - **Who is an admin**: a `private.admins (user_id)` table and `public.is_admin()`, not a role in the JWT, so removing an admin takes effect at once. Admins are added and removed in the Table Editor. - **The server checks every action.** The portal holds only the project URL and publishable key and signs in like the app does. Every admin action is a `public.admin_*` SQL function (`security definer`) whose first step is `private.require_admin()`, which raises `not authorized` (`42501`) for anyone else; execute is granted to `authenticated` only. The `admin` schema and its revokes don't change: the dashboard snippets keep working, and portal functions write `admin.admin_actions` with `performed_by` set explicitly to `auth.uid()::text` (the column defaults to `session_user`, which is `authenticator` for an API call). Rows from the dashboard keep `postgres`; the portal shows them as "Dashboard". The login screen is only UX. - **Sign-in is Google**, the same provider as the app, through Supabase's OAuth redirect. Not email codes: turning on email sign-in on hosted would let anyone create an account by email. Against local Supabase the portal also offers the email code (the code arrives in the local mail viewer, as for the app's dev stub). - **Usage comes from the existing per-user usage tables**, which the Plans section keeps for 40 days and counts on every plan. So the portal shows this month and a 40-day daily series; there's no longer history. Counts only: no prompts, links or names. `ai_calls` still has no user id (6.5). - **Plans are edited as data.** The six feature keys are fixed in code (each is enforced by an Edge Function); the portal combines them into plans and sets their limits. A plan that has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` must have `categorize`, enforced by a trigger so Table Editor edits obey it too. - **`admin/` is its own Yarn project** (own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), not a workspace, so Next.js's React can't clash with Expo's in a hoisted `node_modules`. The root's TypeScript, ESLint, Jest and Metro ignore it. ### Look: "Pantry, back office" Recognisably the app, made for a laptop. Same as the app: Bricolage Grotesque titles (800, −0.025 em) over Figtree, soft white cards on the pale green ground, round initial avatars, light and dark following the system, and DESIGN.md's colours as CSS variables (no hex in components). Different: a deep-green sidebar (the app's `primary`, darkened) with white text and a small "Back office" pill beside "The Perfect Bite"; dense tables with hairline rows and tabular figures; and each AI feature keeps one aisle colour everywhere (usage tiles, charts, plan grid), so it reads at a glance. No floating tab bar, no phone frames. ### Database ### Portal
title: Admins
text: Admins (spec 4.12, 5). New migration: `private.admins (user_id uuid primary key references auth.users on delete cascade, added_at timestamptz not null default now())`, RLS on, every privilege revoked from `public`, `anon`, `authenticated` and `service_role`; insert the owner by email (jgpasch@gmail.com), as the plans migration does, doing nothing if no such account. `public.is_admin() returns boolean` (`stable`, `security definer`, `search_path = ''`): whether `auth.uid()` has a row; false with no user. Execute revoked from `public` and `anon`, granted to `authenticated`. `private.require_admin()` raises `not authorized` with errcode `42501` unless `is_admin()`; the portal functions in the next tasks call it first. `supabase/seed.sql`: the dev user is an admin. title: Portal functions for users
text: Portal functions for users (spec 4.12). New migration, every function `public`, `security definer`, `search_path = ''`, starting with `perform private.require_admin()`, execute revoked from `public`, `anon` and `service_role` and granted to `authenticated`. `admin_list_users(p_search text default null, p_limit integer default 50, p_offset integer default 0)` returns a table of `user_id`, `email`, `display_name`, `created_at`, `last_sign_in_at`, `plan_id`, `plan_assigned` (false when they're on the default), `assigned_at` and `total_count` (the matches before paging): `p_search` matches email or display name case-insensitively, or a user id exactly when it's a uuid (support requests and function logs give ids), newest first, `p_limit` capped at 200. `admin_user_detail(p_user_id uuid) returns jsonb`: the user's fields as above; `plan` (`id`, `name`, `assigned`, `assigned_at`); `first_month` (whether limits are doubled, and when that ends: the same 30-day constant as `private.monthly_limit`, so expose it from there rather than repeating it); `households` (id, name, role, member count, in their household order); `usage`: for each of the six features, `in_plan`, `used` this calendar month (UTC), `limit` from `private.monthly_limit` (null for no limit) and `resets_at` (the first instant of next month); and `plan_history`, the user's `set_user_plan` audit rows, newest first, each with `performed_by` and `performed_by_email` (the admin's email when `performed_by` is a user id that still exists, else null). Unknown id raises `user not found` (`P0002`). The month's usage per feature comes from one helper, `private.monthly_usage(p_user_id uuid, p_feature text) returns integer` (categorize sums LLM-bound names; the rest count calls; read each usage table's columns from the migrations); if the Plans section's check functions already sum the month with such a helper, use theirs instead of adding a second. `admin_set_user_plan(p_user_id uuid, p_plan_id text, p_note text) returns jsonb`: a null `p_plan_id` deletes their `user_plans` row (back to the default); otherwise upserts it. Raises `user not found`, `plan not found` (`P0002`) and `note required` (`22023`, for a null or blank note), changing nothing. Writes one `admin.admin_actions` row (`action` `set_user_plan`, the user id, `details` `{ from, to }` with plan ids or null for the default, the note, `performed_by` the admin's id) and returns `details`. Setting the plan they're already on still writes the row. pgTAP: each function raises `42501` for a signed-in non-admin, and `anon` and `service_role` can't execute them; search and paging, and search by a user's id; a defaulted user reads `plan_assigned` false; `usage` counts only this month's rows and shows plus's limits doubled for a 10-day-old account; setting a plan and setting null each write one audit row with the admin's id; an unknown plan or blank note changes nothing. Update spec 4.12 (the portal changes a user's plan through `admin_set_user_plan`; the Table Editor still works but isn't audited) and `docs/admin.md`'s "Change a user's plan".
notes: Portal functions for users (2026-10-18, spec 4.12): DONE, checked off. New migration `20261115120000_admin_users.sql`: `public.admin_list_users(p_search, p_limit, p_offset)` (email or display name case-insensitively via `strpos`, so `%` and `_` are literal; a uuid-shaped search matches the id exactly; trimmed; newest first; limit capped at 200, negatives floored at 0; `total_count` via `count(*) over ()`; unassigned users show the default plan with `plan_assigned` false), `public.admin_user_detail(p_user_id)` (fields, `plan`, `first_month` `{ doubled, ends_at }`, `households` in `position` order with role and `member_count`, `usage` as an array of `{ feature, in_plan, used, limit, resets_at }` in the fixed feature order from the existing `private.monthly_usage` (reused, not duplicated) and `private.monthly_limit`, `plan_history` newest first with `performed_by_email` only when `performed_by` is the uuid of an existing user; `user not found` P0002) and `public.admin_set_user_plan(p_user_id, p_plan_id, p_note)` (upserts or deletes `user_plans`; `user not found` / `plan not found` P0002, `note required` 22023; one audit row with `target_plan_id`, `{ from, to }`, the note and `performed_by` = `auth.uid()`). All `security definer`, `search_path = ''`, `require_admin()` first, execute revoked from public/anon/service_role and granted to authenticated. The 30-day constant moved into a new `private.first_month_ends_at(user)`, and `private.monthly_limit` was replaced to use it (same behaviour; the 2× factor stays there). New helper `private.feature_keys()` gives the six keys in order. Docs: spec 4.12 (the first-month constant; changing a plan through the portal and the three functions; the Table Editor still works but isn't audited) and `docs/admin.md` "Change a user's plan". Tests: new pgTAP `50_admin_users.test.sql` (55 checks: privileges for anon/service_role/authenticated, first_month_ends_at and monthly_limit doubling, 42501 for a non-admin on each function and for anon, search by email, name and id, trimming, literal wildcards, paging and `total_count`, the 200 cap over 205 users, defaulted vs assigned plan, the detail's plan, first month, usage counting only this month with plus's limits doubled for a 10-day-old account, categorize in names, features not in the plan, household order, set / null / same plan each writing one audit row with the admin's id, an unknown plan, blank or null note and unknown user changing nothing, plan_history order and emails). Checks: jest (5188 passed), lint, tsc, `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1448 passed). No existing tests changed. No real AI calls. HOSTED STEP (by hand): `supabase db push`.

title: Portal function for AI usage
text: Portal function for AI usage (spec 4.12). In a new migration, like the last task's functions: `admin_ai_usage() returns jsonb` with, for each of the six features, `used` this calendar month across everyone, `users` (how many used it), `daily` (one entry per UTC day for the last 40 days, zeros included, oldest first) and `top_users` (the 10 heaviest this month: user id, email, plan id, `used`, `limit`). Built on `private.monthly_usage` and the usage tables, so the units match `admin_user_detail`. Also `calls`, from `public.ai_calls` (kept 30 days, no user id) over the last 30 days, one entry per `task` as stored (tasks aren't features one-to-one, so don't map them): `total`, a count per `status`, `fallbacks` (rows with `fallback_of` set) and the sums of `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens`, with the same per `model`. Counts and sums only: never `instructions`, `prompt`, `output` or `response_text`. pgTAP: `42501` for a non-admin; totals, user counts and top users over a few users and days; the daily series has 40 entries, with 0 for days that have no rows; units for categorize are names; `calls` counts statuses, fallbacks and token sums over a few `ai_calls` rows and skips rows older than 30 days.
notes: Portal function for AI usage (2026-10-18, spec 4.12): DONE, checked off. New migration `20261116120000_admin_ai_usage.sql`: `private.daily_usage(feature, since)` (each user's usage per UTC day from the usage tables in the limits' units; now the one place a feature maps to its table and column, and `private.monthly_usage` was replaced as a SQL function over it, same behaviour), `private.ai_call_stats(task, model, since)` (total, every status's count with zeros, fallbacks, the four token sums with nulls as 0) and `public.admin_ai_usage() returns jsonb` (`security definer`, `search_path = ''`, `require_admin()` first, execute only for authenticated; read-only, no audit row): `{ month_start, features: [{ feature, used, users, daily: [{ day, used }] x40 oldest first, top_users: [{ user_id, email, plan_id, used, limit }] up to 10 by used desc then id }], calls_since, calls: [{ task, total, statuses, fallbacks, *_tokens, models: [same per model, by name] }] by task }`. `users` and `top_users` skip users whose month sums to 0 (a refused request leaves a 0 row). Never reads instructions/prompt/output/response_text. Spec 4.12 gained an "AI usage" bullet. Tests: new pgTAP `51_admin_ai_usage.test.sql` (27 checks: privileges of the function and helpers, monthly_usage through daily_usage, 42501 for a non-admin and anon, feature order, month totals and user counts, a 0 row not counting as a user, the 40-day series ending today with zeros, a last-month day in it and a 41-day-old row out, the top-10 cap, ordering with ties by id, default vs assigned plan and a null limit for a feature not in the plan, categorize in names, an unused feature all zeros, calls per task skipping rows over 30 days, status counts, fallbacks, token sums, the per-model breakdown, no prompt text in the answer). Checks: jest (5188 passed), lint, tsc, `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1475 passed). No existing tests changed. No real AI calls. HOSTED STEP (by hand): `supabase db push`.

text: Portal functions for plans (spec 4.12, 5). New migration. **Rule**: a constraint trigger (`deferrable initially deferred`) on `plan_features` raises `recipe import needs categorize` (`23514`) when a plan ends a transaction with `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` but not `categorize`; replace pgTAP's every-plan check with tests of the trigger (insert, delete of `categorize`, and adding both in one transaction is fine). Functions, like the user ones (admin check, audit row with `performed_by`, a required note, raising and changing nothing on any error): `admin_list_plans() returns jsonb` (each plan's id, name, `is_default`, `users` (assigned plus, for the default, everyone unassigned), and its features with `monthly_limit`, in the features' fixed order); `admin_create_plan(p_id, p_name, p_copy_from default null, p_note)` (id `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,30}$` and unused; copies the source's `plan_features` and `plan_limits`; never copies `is_default`); `admin_rename_plan(p_id, p_name, p_note)`; `admin_set_default_plan(p_id, p_note)` (clears the old default first, for the partial unique index); `admin_set_plan_feature(p_plan_id, p_feature, p_enabled boolean, p_monthly_limit integer default null, p_note)` (enabling adds the feature and an explicit `plan_limits` row with the limit, null for no limit; disabling removes both); `admin_set_plan_limit(p_plan_id, p_feature, p_monthly_limit integer, p_note)` (the feature must be in the plan; null for no limit; `>= 0`); `admin_delete_plan(p_id, p_note)` (refuses the default plan with `default plan` and a plan with `user_plans` rows with `plan in use`, both `23503`). Unknown feature keys are refused by the existing check. Each audit row's `action` is the function's name without `admin_`, with `target_plan_id` the plan id and `details` the before and after and the number of users affected. pgTAP: non-admins get `42501`; copy gives identical features and limits; the trigger's message comes through when removing `categorize` from a plan with import; disabling a feature removes its limit row; a limit change shows at once in `private.monthly_limit`; delete refusals; each success writes one audit row. Update spec 4.12 (plans are edited from the portal; the rule is a trigger; the feature keys stay fixed in code) and section 5; `docs/admin.md` (the Table Editor still works, unaudited, and the trigger applies there too).
notes: Portal functions for plans (2026-10-18, spec 4.12, 5): DONE, checked off. New migration `20261117120000_admin_plans.sql`: constraint trigger `plan_features_import_needs_categorize` (`after insert or update or delete`, `deferrable initially deferred`, function `private.check_import_needs_categorize`) raising `recipe import needs categorize` (`23514`) when a touched plan (old and new plan_id) has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` but not `categorize`; it checks the plan as it is now, not the row. Functions (`security definer`, `search_path = ''`, `require_admin()` first, execute only for authenticated): `admin_list_plans()` (by id; `id`, `name`, `is_default`, `users`, `features` [{ feature, monthly_limit }] in `private.feature_keys()` order), `admin_create_plan`, `admin_rename_plan`, `admin_set_default_plan` (details also has `previous_default`), `admin_set_plan_feature`, `admin_set_plan_limit` (`feature not in plan` P0002), `admin_delete_plan` (`default plan` / `plan in use` 23503). Other errors: `plan not found` P0002, `note required` / `name required` / `invalid plan id` 22023, `plan exists` 23505. Each success writes one audit row (`action` without `admin_`, `target_plan_id`, `details` { before, after, users } from the new `private.plan_snapshot` / `private.plan_user_count`) and returns the details. New helpers: `private.log_plan_action` (runs `set constraints … immediate` then `deferred`, so a broken rule raises from the call, not at commit), `private.lock_plan` and `private.require_note`. No client can execute any of them. Two choices the task didn't spell out: Postgres requires every param after a defaulted one to have a default, so `p_note` in `admin_create_plan` and `admin_set_plan_feature` is `default null` and still required (raises `note required`); disabling a feature the plan doesn't have changes nothing but still writes its audit row (as `set_user_plan` does when the plan doesn't change). Tests: CHANGED EXISTING `17_plans.test.sql` as the task asked: replaced the every-plan check with 11 trigger tests (deferrable/initially deferred in pg_trigger; inserting recipe_import or recipe_import_photo, deleting categorize and moving categorize off by update are all refused; deleting categorize from a plan without import is fine; recipe_import then categorize in one transaction is fine; deferred, the rule can be broken mid-transaction but the check refuses it; fixing it in the same transaction passes) (48 → 58). New `52_admin_plans.test.sql` (77 checks: privileges for anon/service_role/authenticated and the helpers; 42501 for a non-admin on all seven and for no user, changing nothing; list order, the default's user count, fixed feature order with limits, empty and null limits; a copy gives identical features and limits and is never the default; id format edges (capitals, 1 char, leading digit and 32 chars refused, 31 fine), used id, unknown source, blank name or note; rename; enabling with a limit, with null (explicit row), and again (replaces the limit); disabling removes the limit row; the trigger's message through set_plan_feature both ways; unknown feature and negative limit 23514; set_plan_limit shows at once in private.monthly_limit, null lifts it, a missing row is created, feature not in plan; set default moves unassigned users at once, leaves one default, returns previous_default; delete refusals and cascade; one audit row per success by action, none for refusals). goal: Goal: a small web app, run locally against hosted Supabase, for the jobs the dashboard makes awkward: find a user and change their plan, edit what each plan includes and its monthly limits, and see how much of each AI feature people use. It lives in `admin/` in this repo. The dashboard and the `admin.*` SQL snippets stay for everything else (deleting a user, reading logs). ### Decisions - **Who is an admin**: a `private.admins (user_id)` table and `public.is_admin()`, not a role in the JWT, so removing an admin takes effect at once. Admins are added and removed in the Table Editor. - **The server checks every action.** The portal holds only the project URL and publishable key and signs in like the app does. Every admin action is a `public.admin_*` SQL function (`security definer`) whose first step is `private.require_admin()`, which raises `not authorized` (`42501`) for anyone else; execute is granted to `authenticated` only. The `admin` schema and its revokes don't change: the dashboard snippets keep working, and portal functions write `admin.admin_actions` with `performed_by` set explicitly to `auth.uid()::text` (the column defaults to `session_user`, which is `authenticator` for an API call). Rows from the dashboard keep `postgres`; the portal shows them as "Dashboard". The login screen is only UX. - **Sign-in is Google**, the same provider as the app, through Supabase's OAuth redirect. Not email codes: turning on email sign-in on hosted would let anyone create an account by email. Against local Supabase the portal also offers the email code (the code arrives in the local mail viewer, as for the app's dev stub). - **Usage comes from the existing per-user usage tables**, which the Plans section keeps for 40 days and counts on every plan. So the portal shows this month and a 40-day daily series; there's no longer history. Counts only: no prompts, links or names. `ai_calls` still has no user id (6.5). - **Plans are edited as data.** The six feature keys are fixed in code (each is enforced by an Edge Function); the portal combines them into plans and sets their limits. A plan that has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` must have `categorize`, enforced by a trigger so Table Editor edits obey it too. - **`admin/` is its own Yarn project** (own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), not a workspace, so Next.js's React can't clash with Expo's in a hoisted `node_modules`. The root's TypeScript, ESLint, Jest and Metro ignore it. ### Look: "Pantry, back office" Recognisably the app, made for a laptop. Same as the app: Bricolage Grotesque titles (800, −0.025 em) over Figtree, soft white cards on the pale green ground, round initial avatars, light and dark following the system, and DESIGN.md's colours as CSS variables (no hex in components). Different: a deep-green sidebar (the app's `primary`, darkened) with white text and a small "Back office" pill beside "The Perfect Bite"; dense tables with hairline rows and tabular figures; and each AI feature keeps one aisle colour everywhere (usage tiles, charts, plan grid), so it reads at a glance. No floating tab bar, no phone frames. ### Database ### Portal
title: Portal function for activity
text: Portal function for activity (spec 4.12). In a new migration, like the others: `admin_list_actions(p_action text default null, p_limit integer default 50, p_offset integer default 0) returns jsonb`: `admin.admin_actions` newest first (every action: the portal's, the dashboard snippets' `delete_user`, the app's `delete_account`), each with `id`, `action`, `target_user_id` and that user's email if they still exist, `target_household_id`, `target_plan_id`, `details`, `note`, `performed_by`, `performed_by_email` (as in `admin_user_detail`) and `created_at`, plus `total_count`; `p_action` filters to one action; `p_limit` capped at 200. pgTAP: `42501` for a non-admin; order, filter and paging; a `postgres` row has a null `performed_by_email`; a deleted target user's email is null.
notes: Portal function for activity (spec 4.12): new migration `20261118120000_admin_actions.sql` with `public.admin_list_actions(p_action default null, p_limit default 50, p_offset default 0) returns jsonb` (`security definer`, `require_admin()` first, execute for `authenticated` only): `{ actions, total_count }`, every `admin.admin_actions` row newest first (ties by id), or only `p_action`'s (a blank one is no filter), `p_limit` capped at 200, each with `id`, `action`, `target_user_id`, `target_user_email` (null once the user is gone), `target_household_id`, `target_plan_id`, `details`, `note`, `performed_by`, `performed_by_email` (as in `admin_user_detail`, but the uuid cast sits in a `case` so a non-uuid `performed_by` is never cast) and `created_at`. Choice the task didn't spell out: the target's email key is `target_user_email`. New pgTAP `53_admin_actions.test.sql` (33 checks: privileges for anon/service_role/authenticated; 42501 for a non-admin and for no user; total, default page 50, 200 cap, last page, limit 0 keeps the total; newest first across delete_user/delete_account/set_user_plan/rename_plan; offset; filter total, rows, paging within the filter, an unknown action gives `{"actions":[],"total_count":0}`, blank filter; every field of a portal row; a postgres row's null performed_by_email; a deleted target keeps its id with a null email; a non-uuid performer and a since-deleted admin id give null emails; listing writes nothing). Spec 4.12: an "Activity" bullet. Checks: `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (52 files, 1595 passed), jest (5188 passed), lint, tsc. No real AI calls. HOSTED STEP (by hand): `supabase db push`.

title: Demo data for local
text: Demo data for local. `supabase/seed-admin-demo.sql`, run by hand (not from `seed.sql`, so pgTAP counts and the app's dev data don't change): about 10 fake `auth.users` (`demo-N@example.com`, display names, joined over the last few months, one under 30 days old) spread over every plan, some with no `user_plans` row; usage rows for every feature spread over the last 40 days, a couple of users at or over plus's limits; a few `ai_calls` rows per task with mixed statuses and tokens (placeholder text for the required text columns); and a few `admin.admin_actions` rows. Idempotent (fixed uuids, `on conflict do nothing`), with a header comment saying how to run it (`psql` on port 55322, or the local SQL editor) and how to remove it. `admin/README.md` (or `docs/admin.md` until the scaffold exists) mentions it. Check it runs twice cleanly after `supabase db reset`.
notes: Demo data for local (2026-10-18): DONE, checked off. New `supabase/seed-admin-demo.sql` (not run by `seed.sql`; one transaction): 10 `auth.users` `demo-1..10@example.com` with fixed ids `de300000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000NN`, `full_name` metadata (so the profile trigger sets display names), joined 12–160 days ago (demo-9 under 30 days), `last_sign_in_at` set, no password or identity; `user_plans` for 7 of them covering none/basic/plus/unlimited, 3 on the default; usage in all six usage tables over the last 40 days for the features in each user's effective plan (from `plan_features`, deterministic `hashtext` values scaled to about a thirtieth of plus's limits), with a top-up row today so demo-1 is exactly at every plus limit and demo-2 (default plan) is 25% over; 48 `ai_calls` (8 per task, every status, tokens, created within 30 days, placeholder `instructions`/`prompt`, `prompt_version` `demo`) plus 6 fallback calls pointing at the `api_error` rows; 5 `admin.admin_actions` (three `set_user_plan` by the dev user's id, a `rename_plan`, a `postgres` `delete_user` of a gone user). `on conflict do nothing` everywhere; header says how to run it (psql on 55322 or the local SQL editor) and the three `delete … where id::text like 'de300000-%'` statements that remove it. `docs/admin.md`: "Demo data for the portal (local only)" (no `admin/` yet). Choices: no identities (demo users aren't for signing in); dates are relative to the run, so a re-run on a later day adds that day's rows. Verification: plain `psql` and `supabase db query` (one statement only) weren't available in this session, so I ran the file through psql inside `supabase test db` (`\ir` twice, each run committing) with 17 pgTAP checks: 10 users and profiles, 7 assignments, 54 calls, 5 actions, identical counts and categorize sums after the second run, all six features have usage, demo-1 = plus limits, demo-2 > plus limits, every plan used, `admin_ai_usage`/`admin_list_users('demo-')` (10)/`admin_list_actions` run as the dev admin; then the header's deletes removed everything (checked: 0 rows left). Then `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (53 files, 1612 passed), jest (5188 passed), lint, tsc. No real AI calls. CLEANUP NEEDED: this session couldn't delete files, so the scratch `supabase/tests/99_tmp_demo.test.sql` and `supabase/tests/seed-admin-demo.tmp` (a copy of the seed without its header) are still there; delete both (they pass, but the copy will drift from the real file).
manualChecks: Users: with `admin/.env.local` on local Supabase and the demo data loaded (`supabase/seed-admin-demo.sql`), `yarn admin`, sign in as the dev admin, open /users: the table shows avatar initial, name, email, plan badge ("Plus · default" for demo users with no plan of their own), joined and last sign-in as relative dates with the full date on hover. Type "demo-" (the URL gets `?q=demo-` after a moment, focus stays in the box); type "zzz" for the no-match state; paste `de300000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` for just that user. With more than 50 users, Next goes to `?page=2` and "51–… of N" shows. Open demo-1 (at every plus limit: bars full in red), demo-9 (under 30 days: the "First month · 2× limits until …" badge and "(2× first month)" in each limited row), a basic or none user ("Not in plan" rows greyed), an unlimited user ("… · no limit", no bars); the Households and Plan history cards (who is an email for the dev admin's changes, "Dashboard" for postgres'). /users/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 and /users/nope say "No such user". Check light and dark.

Change a user's plan: with `admin/.env.local` on local Supabase and the demo data loaded, `yarn admin`, sign in as the dev admin, open a demo user on the default plan (e.g. demo-2). Change plan on the Plan card opens a dialog with Default (Plus) first, marked Current, then every plan with its features and limits on one line; Save is disabled until the Note has text. Pick Basic, note "test", Save: the dialog closes, "Moved demo-2@example.com to Basic" shows at the bottom, the Plan card and badge say Basic, and Plan history has Default (Plus) → Basic. Change plan again, pick Default (Plus), Save: back on the default, with a second history row. /activity (once built) shows both `set_user_plan` rows. An error (delete the user in the SQL editor first, then Save) stays in the dialog with the server's message ("user not found").

AI usage: with `yarn admin` against local Supabase and the demo data, open AI usage (`/ai-usage`). Every feature card has a total in its unit and a users count, and a 40-day bar chart in its colour with today labelled ("Today") and stronger, and a dashed line with the 1st's date (e.g. "Oct 1") before the 1st. Hovering a bar shows e.g. "Oct 3: 12 names". Top users lists emails (each opening that user's page), plan names and used / limit. Under AI calls ("Last 30 days"), the By task and By model tables have calls, failure rates (hovering shows each non-ok status, e.g. "timeout 1"), fallbacks and the four token columns. Check light and dark.

Activity: with `yarn admin` against local Supabase and the demo data, after the Change plan and Plans checks, open `/activity`. Each change shows once, newest first, with the right label, target (a user's email links to their page; a plan shows its id), summary (e.g. "plus → unlimited", "recipe_import limit 40 → 60"), note and who (your email; "Dashboard" for a dashboard `delete_user`). Filter by an action (the URL gets `?action=`; All actions clears it) and page with Previous/Next past 50 rows.

title: Scaffold `admin/` and keep it apart from the app
text: Scaffold `admin/` and keep it apart from the app (spec 4.12). A Next.js App Router app in TypeScript, as its own Yarn project: its own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`. **How, in this repo** (agents can only run commands that start with `yarn`, so never `cd admin && …`): create it from the repo root with `yarn dlx create-next-app@latest admin --ts --tailwind --eslint --app --no-src-dir --use-yarn --skip-install --disable-git --yes`; then write an empty `admin/yarn.lock` (Yarn 4 refuses to install a nested project without one: "isn't part of the project"); then run everything inside it as `yarn --cwd admin <command>` (`install`, `add`, `lint`, `build`, …), and shadcn as `yarn --cwd admin dlx shadcn@latest init --yes --defaults` / `… add <component> --yes`. Read the Next.js docs for the version it installs (nextjs.org; the session gate is `proxy.ts` in current Next.js). Add `@supabase/supabase-js` and `@supabase/ssr` (a browser client and a server client in `admin/lib/supabase/`), and shadcn/ui for dialogs, popovers and inputs. Env: `admin/.env.example` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `.env.local` gitignored; nothing else, and never a secret or service-role key. A placeholder home page is enough for now. Root: `tsconfig.json` excludes `admin`, ESLint ignores `admin/**`, Jest has `<rootDir>/admin/` in both `testPathIgnorePatterns` and `modulePathIgnorePatterns` (so `admin/node_modules` can't collide with the app's), Metro's resolver blocks `admin/` (check the Metro docs for Expo SDK 57), and a root script `admin` that runs the portal's dev server (`yarn --cwd admin dev`). Vitest in `admin/` for pure helpers, with one trivial test; `yarn --cwd admin lint`, `yarn --cwd admin tsc --noEmit`, `yarn --cwd admin test` and `yarn --cwd admin build` pass, and the root's lint, typecheck and Jest still pass. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): an `admin` job beside `app` and `database` that, in `admin/`, runs `yarn install --immutable`, lint, typecheck, test and build. AGENTS.md: a short "Admin portal" section (where it is, `yarn admin` or `yarn --cwd admin dev`, its env, that it's its own Yarn project and isn't Expo, so the Expo rules don't apply there). `admin/README.md`: running it against local and against hosted.

text: Sign-in and the admin gate (spec 4.12). Inside `admin/`, run commands as `yarn --cwd admin <command>`. `/sign-in`: **Continue with Google** (`signInWithOAuth`, redirecting to `/auth/callback`, a route handler that exchanges the code for a session); when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` is local (`127.0.0.1` or `localhost`), also an email and 6-digit code form. `proxy.ts` refreshes the session and sends anyone signed out to `/sign-in`. title: Users
text: Users (spec 4.12). Inside `admin/`, run commands as `yarn --cwd admin <command>`. `/users`: a search box (debounced, kept in `?q=`, with paging in `?page=`, 50 a page), a table of avatar initial, name, email, plan badge ("Plus" or "Plus · default" when unassigned), joined and last sign-in (relative, full date on hover), from `admin_list_users`; empty and no-match states. A row opens `/users/[id]`, from `admin_user_detail`: a header (avatar, name, email, joined, last sign-in, a "First month · 2× limits until <date>" badge when it applies); a **Plan** card (the plan, assigned or default, since when); a **This month** card with one row per feature in its colour: "23 / 40 imports · resets Nov 1" with a bar, "12 names · no limit", or "Not in plan" greyed; **Households** (name, role, members); and **Plan history** (from, to, note, who, when; who is the admin's email, "Dashboard" for `postgres`, else the raw id). Pasting a user id into the search finds that user. Unknown id: "No such user". Vitest: the usage row's wording for a limit, no limit, not in plan and the doubled case; the "who" wording. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: against local with the demo data, search, page, open a user, check each card.
notes: Households docs. `docs/spec.md` §10 now has a "Landed early" note under M5. It lists what was pulled forward: `households` and `household_members` (with RLS), `create_household` and `get_household_members`. It also says the app registers its local household via `registerHouseholds` instead of sign-up creating one on the server, which M5 revisits. A matching note under M7 covers the read-only Households screen: invites, rename, leave, remove and roles are still M7, and `household_invites` doesn't exist yet. `README.md` "Looking at the data" now explains how to add a test member. The second user signs in once so they have a profile, then an `insert ... select` into `household_members` matches both users by email and sets position to their max + 1; the section also shows how to remove them again. I also updated the README's out-of-date sentence saying Supabase only handles sign-in and profiles. No code tests (docs only). jest (276), lint and typecheck pass. **The README SQL wasn't run** because psql needs approval in this session, so check it once in Studio.

Per-user rate limit (spec 6.4), done after the task was reworded to settle the earlier blocker. Migration `20261009230000_categorize_limit.sql`: `private.categorize_usage` (PK user_id+day, FK to auth.users on delete cascade) and `private.categorize_daily_total`, with RLS on and all grants revoked from public/anon/authenticated. `public.check_categorize_limit(p_user_id, p_new_names, p_daily_cap) returns text` is `security definer`, `search_path = ''`, and only service_role can execute it. Days are UTC and the minute is a fixed `date_trunc('minute')` window. It upserts a zero row, then locks the user row and then the day's total `for update`. Counters change only on 'ok'; a refused first request leaves a zero row. A negative or null argument raises 22023. A cron job (`categorize-usage-retention`) deletes old rows. Edge Function: `CategorizeStore.checkLimit(newNames)` calls the RPC. `categorize` calls it once per request, after reading the DB and before writing anything, with the LLM-bound count (0 when AI is off). On a refusal it throws `CategorizeLimitError(reason)`, so a refused request writes no pending rows. `handleRequest` maps `user_limit` to 429 `rate_limited` and `global_cap` to 503 `daily_cap_reached` with `Retry-After: 3600`. `index.ts` builds the store with the user id and `dailyNameCap(CATEGORIZE_DAILY_NAME_CAP)` (default 20,000; invalid values fall back to it). Documented in `supabase/functions/.env.example`. Tests: new pgTAP `07_categorize_limit.test.sql` (35): 60 a minute, then refused even with 0 names; another user unaffected; the window resets; 500/501 names a day, and a batch that crosses the limit is refused whole; refused requests leave counters unchanged; the global cap refuses every user, but 0 new names still gets ok; a null user skips the per-user limits but not the cap and writes no usage row; bad args raise; anon/authenticated can't call the function or read the tables, and service_role can call it. Deno, 10 new (76 pass): checkLimit counts only LLM-bound names; all-known counts 0; off counts 0; user_limit/global_cap refuse with no LLM call and no writes; a check error propagates; 429; 503 + Retry-After; 400 comes before the limit; `dailyNameCap` parsing. The existing FakeStore got a `checkLimit` method; no existing assertions changed. jest (426), lint, tsc, `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` (132) pass. Not checked by hand against the served function: the RPC call in `store.ts` has no automated test.
