DONE (2026-10-10) "Realtime": I chose "trigger a cursor pull per household", so pull stays the only path that applies remote rows. Server: new migration `20261010150000_realtime.sql` adds the 8 household tables, `household_members`, `categories`, the 3 per-user tables and `ingredients` to the `supabase_realtime` publication. Realtime then applies each subscriber's RLS select policies. Replica identity stays the default (primary key). Client: new `src/sync/realtime.ts`, `startRealtime(userId)`, started from `AppDataGate` while signed in. It opens one channel per household (each household table filtered `household_id=eq.<id>`, or `id=eq.` for `households`), a user channel (`household_members` and the user's 4 own tables, filtered to the user) and a catalog channel (`ingredients`). An event schedules a scoped pull. Events within `REALTIME_BATCH_MS` (300 ms) of the first share one pull. A household event pulls that household, a user-table event pulls the user's tables, and a catalog event pulls the catalog. A `household_members` event for this user does a full pull. Each full pull reports the memberships it read through the new `onMemberships`, and channels are opened and closed to match. Each channel pulls its scope once SUBSCRIBED, which covers the gap since the last pull and rejoins after errors. Background or offline closes every channel. Foreground reopens them, and a reconnect replaces them with new ones. An event that arrives on a channel after it has closed is ignored. `pull.ts` changes: `pullNow({ scope })` with `PullScope` (`households`, `user`, `catalog`). A scoped run doesn't read memberships. Coalescing now merges the scopes asked for during a run (`mergeScopes`), and a full request makes the next run full. I also added `applyRemoteDelete`, which fills the gap the pull task left: Realtime DELETE events for the user's `user_category_order`/`user_category_overrides` rows (hard-deleted, so pull can't see them) delete the local row from the event's key, unless the outbox has an unpushed change for it. Delete events can't be filtered, so other users' deletes arrive and are ignored, including other members' `household_members` deletes. The remote check animates like a local one with no UI change: the list's `useLiveQueryOn` re-runs on any SQLite change, and the row's Reanimated layout/entering animations don't care where the write came from. Known gaps for the Membership task: a lost membership only closes that household's channel. Its local rows and outbox entries stay until that task's purge. Household hard-deletes (cascades) just trigger a pull of that household. Spec 7.2 has a "Realtime" client note. Tests added: `src/sync/__tests__/realtime.test.ts` (20), which drives the real pull against a fake server: which channels open and their exact bindings/filters; channels before and after memberships are known; not configured opens none; cleanup closes all and cancels a scheduled pull; a remote check comes down within the batch window through the pull (only that household's 8 tables queried, local item checked); several events share one pull and two households pull both; another household's change isn't delivered; user-table and catalog events pull only those; a deleted override is applied without a pull while another user's delete is ignored; SUBSCRIBED catches up per channel; CHANNEL_ERROR just warns; joining a household does a full pull and opens its channel; losing one closes only that channel; another member's removal is ignored; background/foreground, starting in the background, offline/reconnect (new channels) and staying online (same channels); events on closed channels do nothing. In `pull.test.ts` (13 new): `mergeScopes`; household-, user- and catalog-scoped pulls query exactly those tables; an empty scope; scoped calls during a run merged into one more run; a full request upgrades the next run; `onMemberships` (each full pull, replay for the same user only, scoped pulls silent, unsubscribe, a failed lookup reports nothing); `applyRemoteDelete` (deletes without an outbox write, keeps a row with an unpushed change, ignores another user/missing row/incomplete key/other tables, order rows). Also new: `supabase/tests/09_realtime.test.sql` (exactly these tables published, no private tables, default replica identity). goal: Goal: a small web app, run locally against hosted Supabase, for the jobs the dashboard makes awkward: find a user and change their plan, edit what each plan includes and its monthly limits, and see how much of each AI feature people use. It lives in `admin/` in this repo. The dashboard and the `admin.*` SQL snippets stay for everything else (deleting a user, reading logs). ### Decisions - **Who is an admin**: a `private.admins (user_id)` table and `public.is_admin()`, not a role in the JWT, so removing an admin takes effect at once. Admins are added and removed in the Table Editor. - **The server checks every action.** The portal holds only the project URL and publishable key and signs in like the app does. Every admin action is a `public.admin_*` SQL function (`security definer`) whose first step is `private.require_admin()`, which raises `not authorized` (`42501`) for anyone else; execute is granted to `authenticated` only. The `admin` schema and its revokes don't change: the dashboard snippets keep working, and portal functions write `admin.admin_actions` with `performed_by` set explicitly to `auth.uid()::text` (the column defaults to `session_user`, which is `authenticator` for an API call). Rows from the dashboard keep `postgres`; the portal shows them as "Dashboard". The login screen is only UX. - **Sign-in is Google**, the same provider as the app, through Supabase's OAuth redirect. Not email codes: turning on email sign-in on hosted would let anyone create an account by email. Against local Supabase the portal also offers the email code (the code arrives in the local mail viewer, as for the app's dev stub). - **Usage comes from the existing per-user usage tables**, which the Plans section keeps for 40 days and counts on every plan. So the portal shows this month and a 40-day daily series; there's no longer history. Counts only: no prompts, links or names. `ai_calls` still has no user id (6.5). - **Plans are edited as data.** The six feature keys are fixed in code (each is enforced by an Edge Function); the portal combines them into plans and sets their limits. A plan that has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` must have `categorize`, enforced by a trigger so Table Editor edits obey it too. - **`admin/` is its own Yarn project** (own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), not a workspace, so Next.js's React can't clash with Expo's in a hoisted `node_modules`. The root's TypeScript, ESLint, Jest and Metro ignore it. ### Look: "Pantry, back office" Recognisably the app, made for a laptop. Same as the app: Bricolage Grotesque titles (800, −0.025 em) over Figtree, soft white cards on the pale green ground, round initial avatars, light and dark following the system, and DESIGN.md's colours as CSS variables (no hex in components). Different: a deep-green sidebar (the app's `primary`, darkened) with white text and a small "Back office" pill beside "The Perfect Bite"; dense tables with hairline rows and tabular figures; and each AI feature keeps one aisle colour everywhere (usage tiles, charts, plan grid), so it reads at a glance. No floating tab bar, no phone frames. ### Database ### Portal

goal: Goal: a small web app, run locally against hosted Supabase, for the jobs the dashboard makes awkward: find a user and change their plan, edit what each plan includes and its monthly limits, and see how much of each AI feature people use. It lives in `admin/` in this repo. The dashboard and the `admin.*` SQL snippets stay for everything else (deleting a user, reading logs). ### Decisions - **Who is an admin**: a `private.admins (user_id)` table and `public.is_admin()`, not a role in the JWT, so removing an admin takes effect at once. Admins are added and removed in the Table Editor. - **The server checks every action.** The portal holds only the project URL and publishable key and signs in like the app does. Every admin action is a `public.admin_*` SQL function (`security definer`) whose first step is `private.require_admin()`, which raises `not authorized` (`42501`) for anyone else; execute is granted to `authenticated` only. The `admin` schema and its revokes don't change: the dashboard snippets keep working, and portal functions write `admin.admin_actions` with `performed_by` set explicitly to `auth.uid()::text` (the column defaults to `session_user`, which is `authenticator` for an API call). Rows from the dashboard keep `postgres`; the portal shows them as "Dashboard". The login screen is only UX. - **Sign-in is Google**, the same provider as the app, through Supabase's OAuth redirect. Not email codes: turning on email sign-in on hosted would let anyone create an account by email. Against local Supabase the portal also offers the email code (the code arrives in the local mail viewer, as for the app's dev stub). - **Usage comes from the existing per-user usage tables**, which the Plans section keeps for 40 days and counts on every plan. So the portal shows this month and a 40-day daily series; there's no longer history. Counts only: no prompts, links or names. `ai_calls` still has no user id (6.5). - **Plans are edited as data.** The six feature keys are fixed in code (each is enforced by an Edge Function); the portal combines them into plans and sets their limits. A plan that has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` must have `categorize`, enforced by a trigger so Table Editor edits obey it too. - **`admin/` is its own Yarn project** (own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), not a workspace, so Next.js's React can't clash with Expo's in a hoisted `node_modules`. The root's TypeScript, ESLint, Jest and Metro ignore it. ### Look: "Pantry, back office" Recognisably the app, made for a laptop. Same as the app: Bricolage Grotesque titles (800, −0.025 em) over Figtree, soft white cards on the pale green ground, round initial avatars, light and dark following the system, and DESIGN.md's colours as CSS variables (no hex in components). Different: a deep-green sidebar (the app's `primary`, darkened) with white text and a small "Back office" pill beside "The Perfect Bite"; dense tables with hairline rows and tabular figures; and each AI feature keeps one aisle colour everywhere (usage tiles, charts, plan grid), so it reads at a glance. No floating tab bar, no phone frames. ### Database ### Portal

Precedence: signed out "Not syncing" > offline "Offline" > push/pull running "Syncing…" > a standing push/pull error "Sync error" (push first, shown as "Sending: …" / "Receiving: …") > pending outbox "Syncing…" > never synced "Not synced yet" > "Synced". The file also has `formatLastSync`, `outboxCounts` (pending vs rejected), `readSyncInputs` and `syncNow` (a forced push, then a full pull). The filter is `components/action-filter.tsx`, a client `<select>` that does `router.replace` to `?action=` and goes back to page 1; an unknown `?action=` is kept as an extra option. The wording is in `admin/lib/activity.ts`. Labels: Changed plan, Changed a limit, Changed a feature, Created a plan, Renamed a plan, Changed the default plan, Deleted a plan, Deleted user, Deleted own account, and the raw name for anything else. Target: the user's email linking to `/users/[id]`, else the plan id, else the household id; then (my addition) a deleted user's raw id, unlinked; else "—". Summaries: set_user_plan "plus → unlimited" (null as "default"); set_plan_limit and set_plan_feature from the before/after snapshots ("recipe_import limit 40 → 60", "recipe_tags added, limit no limit", "recipe_import removed", "No change"; raw feature keys, as in the task's example); create_plan "“Pro” · 2 features"; rename_plan "“Plus” → “Plus+”"; set_default_plan "base → plus" ("none" when there was no default); delete_plan "“Old” · 0 users"; delete_user "<email> · 3 households: 1 promoted, 2 deleted"; delete_account "1 household: 1 left"; an unknown action shows its details as compact JSON cut to 80 characters. Who: the admin's email, "Dashboard" for `postgres`, otherwise the raw value. One choice of mine: `delete_account` shows "The user", because the app's row has `performed_by` set to the session user (e.g. `authenticator`). Paging reuses `parsePage`, `parseQuery` and `pageRange` from `lib/users.ts`. Vitest `admin/lib/activity.test.ts` (22 tests) covers: every label and an unknown one (including `toString`); filter options; URLs; each action's summary with edge cases (null default, no limit, thousands, no change, added/removed, singulars, no households, malformed details) and the unknown one (JSON, truncation, empty); the target's order and fallbacks; who. Checks: portal test (139 passed), lint, tsc, build; root jest (5203 passed), lint, tsc. Not run against a dev server or local Supabase. No real AI calls. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK (in manual-checks.md).
manualChecks: The portal's look and shell: run `yarn admin` and open http://localhost:3000 (it goes to /users) in a browser with the system in light, then dark. Check: the deep-green sidebar with the gold cloche, "The Perfect Bite" in Bricolage Grotesque and the "Back office" pill on one line; Users, Plans, AI usage and Activity each open their empty page, titled in Bricolage 800 on the pale green ground, with the current one highlighted in the sidebar; body text is Figtree.

goal: Goal: see why AI calls fail, and find people misusing the AI, e.g. a fake recipe written to get an explicit AI photo, with who did it and exactly what we sent the model. `public.ai_calls` already has one row per model attempt by `runAiTask`, with its `status`, `error`, instructions and prompt, but no user id (by design until now), a provider error keeps only the SDK's message, the AI photo's image call (`generateImage`, OpenAI Images) isn't recorded at all, and the portal shows only counts. A photo description that answers `isFood: false` is an `ok` call, so it has to be flagged on purpose, not found among the failures. The spec changes with this: `ai_calls` now records who made each call, and admins can read any call's instructions, prompt and response in the portal (each read is audited) and see the AI photos that were made, since a harmful photo the image model allowed is never flagged. Rows still expire after 30 days, except flagged calls and the calls linked to them, kept 180 days. Emailing the owner about flags (Resend) comes later; not in these tasks.
title: `ai_calls` records who made each call
text: `ai_calls` records who made each call (spec 5, 6.4, 6.5). Migration: add `user_id uuid references auth.users on delete set null` and `household_id uuid references public.households on delete set null` to `public.ai_calls`, with an index on `(user_id, created_at desc)`. Add both to `AiCallRecord` (`supabase/functions/_shared/ai/run-ai-task.ts`) and a `RunAiTaskOptions.caller?: { userId: string; householdId: string | null }` that `runAiTask` copies onto every attempt's record (null without it). Every function that calls a model passes the signed-in caller it already resolves for its feature and limit checks, and the household when the request has one: `categorize-ingredients` (including categorizing inside `import-recipe` and `import-recipe-photo`), `import-recipe`, `import-recipe-photo`, `match-recipe-steps`, `suggest-recipe-tags`, `generate-recipe-photo` (`describeRecipePhoto`). The `yarn ai:*` scripts and evals pass nothing, so their rows have nulls. Deno tests: each handler's test checks its logged rows carry the user (and household where there is one); `runAiTask` with no `caller` records nulls. pgTAP: deleting a user nulls `user_id` and keeps the row. Update spec 5 and 6.4 (the `ai_calls` lines) and 6.5 and every "`ai_calls` stores … but no user id" Privacy line (6.6–6.11): rows now have the user and household, are still service role only, and still expire after 30 days. In `docs/alpha-testing.md`, the privacy policy line also says the policy must disclose that what's sent to the AI is logged with the account and kept 30 days (180 for flagged calls), and that admins can read it.
notes: `ai_calls` records who made each call (2026-10-19, spec 5, 6.4, 6.5): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261119120000_ai_calls_caller.sql` adds `user_id` (→ `auth.users`, on delete set null) and `household_id` (→ `households`, on delete set null) with an index on `(user_id, created_at desc)`. `run-ai-task.ts` exports `AiCaller = { userId, householdId | null }`; `AiCallRecord` gains `user_id`/`household_id`, and `RunAiTaskOptions.caller?` is copied onto every attempt (primary and fallback, ok or failed), nulls without it. Wiring: `categorize(names, store, model?, caller?)` (a 4th positional parameter, so the 45 existing `categorize(…, store, model)` calls didn't change); `caller?` on `ImportDeps`, `PhotoImportDeps`, `SuggestDeps`, `MatchDeps`/`MatchStepsDeps` and `DescribeOptions`; `GenerateDeps.userId?`, with the household taken from the reservation. Each `index.ts` passes `{ userId, householdId: null }` (only AI photos have a household), and import-recipe / import-recipe-photo pass it to the inline categorize too. CLIs and evals pass nothing, so their rows have nulls. Updated the "no user id" comments in the stores, spec 5 (server-only tables), 6.4's Privacy bullet, 6.5 (a new paragraph on `ai_calls`), the Privacy lines of 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 6.10 and 6.11, `docs/admin.md`, and the privacy policy line in `docs/alpha-testing.md` (logged with the account, 30 days, 180 for flagged calls, admins can read it). Existing tests changed because the behavior changed: `06_ai_calls.test.sql` checked `hasnt_column user_id`; it now checks the columns, nullability, the index and the FK, that deleting the user nulls `user_id` and keeps the row and its household, and that deleting the household nulls `household_id` and keeps the user (plan 9 → 20). The suggest-recipe-tags and match-recipe-steps "no user id" tests asserted `!('user_id' in call)`; they now assert the caller's user id and a null household. `categorize-ingredients/cli.test.ts`'s record fixture got the two fields. New Deno tests: `ai.test.ts` (the caller on both the failed primary and the fallback; a caller with no household; no caller gives nulls on ok and on failure), categorize `handler.test.ts` (caller on ok and invalid_output rows; nulls without one), import-recipe and import-recipe-photo (the extraction and inline categorize rows carry the user with a null household; photo import also a failed extraction), suggest-recipe-tags and match-recipe-steps (a failed call carries the caller too), generate-recipe-photo (the description row has the user and the recipe's household, a failed description too, nulls with no caller). Checks: Deno tests in categorize-ingredients (295), import-recipe (177), import-recipe-photo (64), match-recipe-steps (61), suggest-recipe-tags (59), generate-recipe-photo (51), all pass; every edited `index.ts`, CLI and eval type-checks; `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` (1623 passed); root jest (5205 passed), lint, tsc. No real AI calls.

title: Failed AI calls keep the provider's answer
text: Failed AI calls keep the provider's answer (spec 5, 6.4). Migration: add `http_status integer` and `error_body text` to `public.ai_calls` (null on `ok` rows and on failures with no HTTP answer). In `run-ai-task.ts`, add both to `AiCallRecord`; a failed attempt sets `http_status` from `apiCallError(err)?.statusCode` and `error_body` from its `responseBody` (cut to 4000 characters), and `error` keeps its current `name: message` text (2000). Deno tests: a mock model that throws an `APICallError` (status 529, a JSON body) records both; one wrapped in a `RetryError` records the last error's; invalid output and a timeout record nulls; an `ok` attempt records nulls. Safety blocks: find out from the AI SDK provider source (`@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/openai` as the functions import them) how a blocked call comes back for the providers we use: Gemini's blocked prompt (`promptFeedback.blockReason`) or `SAFETY` finish, and an OpenAI structured-output `refusal`. Every such attempt, whatever its status, records `finish_reason` `content-filter` (map it in `runAiTask` if the SDK reports it another way or loses it on a thrown error), so the flag in the task below catches it. Deno tests: a mock model reproducing each shape records `content-filter`. Say in spec 6.4 how a safety block is recorded.
notes: Failed AI calls keep the provider's answer (2026-10-19, spec 5, 6.4): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261120120000_ai_calls_error_body.sql` adds `http_status integer` and `error_body text` to `ai_calls`. `AiCallRecord` gains both; a failed attempt takes them from `apiCallError(err)` (an `APICallError`, or a `RetryError`'s last one): `statusCode` and `responseBody` cut to 4000; `error` is unchanged (`name: message`, 2000); ok rows and failures with no HTTP answer have nulls. Safety blocks: the provider source wasn't readable from the sandbox (the Deno npm cache is outside the repo), so I ran the real `@ai-sdk/google@4.0.88`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic@4.0.72` and `@ai-sdk/openai@4.0.96` against a fake `fetch` returning blocked bodies in a throwaway Deno test. Gemini's `promptFeedback.blockReason` (SAFETY, PROHIBITED_CONTENT) and `SAFETY`/`PROHIBITED_CONTENT` candidate finishes, and Anthropic's `stop_reason: 'refusal'`, all come back as finish reason `content-filter` (raw = the provider's reason) with no output, which `runAiTask` already turns into an `invalid_output` row that keeps the finish reason, so no mapping was needed (a comment says so). The task names `@ai-sdk/openai`, but no function imports it: the language-model providers are Google and Anthropic, and OpenAI is only the image call's plain `fetch` (next task). For the record, `@ai-sdk/openai` reports a chat `refusal` as finish `stop` with empty text and drops the refusal; I didn't map that, since mapping "empty + stop" to `content-filter` would wrongly flag other empty answers and the shape can't reach `runAiTask`. Spec 5 (`ai_calls` line) and 6.4 (new "What a failed attempt records" and "Safety blocks" bullets) say all this. Tests: Deno `categorize-ingredients/ai.test.ts` gets an APICallError 529 with a JSON body records both columns and the error text; a long body/error is cut to 4000/2000; no body gives a status and a null body; a RetryError (503 then 529) records the last error's; invalid output, a timeout (`TimeoutError`) and an ok attempt record nulls; five mock shapes reproducing the probed safety blocks (Gemini blocked prompt, prohibited prompt, SAFETY finish, SAFETY after partial JSON, Anthropic refusal) each record `invalid_output` + `content-filter`; a safety block doesn't try the fallback. `cli.test.ts`'s record helper gets the two new fields (type change only). pgTAP `06_ai_calls`: both columns' types, nulls when unset, and a failed row stores 529 and its body (plan 20 → 25). Deno suites: categorize-ingredients (308), import-recipe (177), import-recipe-photo (64), match-recipe-steps (61), suggest-recipe-tags (59), generate-recipe-photo (51), all pass; `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` pass; root jest (5205 passed), lint, tsc pass. No real AI calls (the probe used a fake fetch). Cleanup needed: the sandbox wouldn't let me delete the scratch files `.probe/probe.ts` and `supabase/functions/categorize-ingredients/zz-probe.test.ts` (emptied); delete both, they aren't part of the change.

title: The AI photo's image call goes into `ai_calls`
text: The AI photo's image call goes into `ai_calls` (spec 6.11, 6.4). Add `refused` to the `ai_calls.status` check, to `private.ai_call_stats`'s `statuses` (zeros included) and to the portal's `AiCallStatus` / `STATUS_ORDER` (`admin/lib/types.ts`, `admin/lib/ai-usage.ts`). In `supabase/functions/generate-recipe-photo/image.ts`, `ImageFailedError` and `ImageRefusedError` carry the HTTP status and the response body when there was one. `handler.ts` logs one row per image call through `store.logAiCall`, success or failure, with the caller as above: `task` `recipePhotoImage`, `model` named the way the other rows name theirs, `prompt_version` `RECIPE_PHOTO_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION`, `instructions` empty, `prompt` the image prompt, `output` `{ quality, path }` on success (the photo's Storage path in `recipe-photos`; never the image bytes), the token counts from `usage`, `duration_ms`, `fallback_of` the description row's id (so the two steps link), and on failure `error`, `http_status` and `error_body` (4000). Status: a content-policy refusal `refused`; an HTTP error `api_error`; the timeout `timeout`; no image or bad base64 `invalid_output`; anything else (no key, `off`) `error`. Both AI photo rows (description and image) also record the recipe: migration adds `recipe_id uuid references public.recipes on delete set null` to `public.ai_calls`, `AiCallRecord` gains it and `RunAiTaskOptions.recipeId?` is copied onto each attempt like `caller` (null for every other task). The mock model logs too. A failure to log never fails the request (log it, like `ai_call_log_failed`). pgTAP: `refused` is accepted and counted by `ai_call_stats`. Deno tests (`generate-recipe-photo/handler.test.ts`): a generated photo logs the description row and an `ok` image row linked to it, both with the recipe id, the image row with the photo's path; a refusal, a 500 and a timeout each log the right status with the HTTP status and body; the image bytes are never in a row. Update spec 6.4 ("one row per model attempt") and 6.11's Privacy line. (If `fallback_of` reads wrong for the link, add a `parent_id` column instead and say so in the spec.)
notes: The AI photo's image call goes into `ai_calls` (2026-10-19, spec 6.4, 6.11): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261121120000_ai_calls_image.sql`: `refused` added to the `ai_calls.status` check; `recipe_id uuid references public.recipes on delete set null`; `private.ai_call_stats` counts `refused` (zeros included) and leaves `recipePhotoImage` rows out of `fallbacks`, since their `fallback_of` is the link to the description, not a fallback. I kept `fallback_of` for the link (no `parent_id`), as the next tasks' retention and `primary`/`fallback` build on it; the spec says so. `run-ai-task.ts`: `AiCallRecord` gains `recipe_id`, `task` may be `RECIPE_PHOTO_IMAGE_TASK` (`recipePhotoImage`), status may be `refused`; `RunAiTaskOptions.recipeId?` is copied onto each attempt (null otherwise). `image.ts`: `ImageRefusedError` and `ImageFailedError` carry `httpStatus` and `body` (the raw text of a failed answer; a 200's body is never kept, since it holds the image), and `ImageFailedError.failure` is the row's status (HTTP or network error `api_error`, timeout `timeout`, no image/bad base64 `invalid_output`, no key/`off` `error`); new `imageModelId` (`openai:<model>`, `mock` stays `mock`). `describe.ts` takes `recipeId` and returns the answering row's `callId`. `handler.ts` writes one `recipePhotoImage` row per image call (success, refusal, failure) with the caller, household, recipe, empty instructions, the image prompt, `{ quality, path }` on success (the row is written before the upload), tokens, duration, `fallback_of` the description row, and `error`/`http_status`/`error_body` (4000) on failure. A failed write logs `ai_call_log_failed` and never fails the request. Portal: `AiCallStatus`/`STATUS_ORDER` gain `refused` (between timeout and error). Spec: 5 (`ai_calls` line: image rows, statuses, `recipe_id`), 4.12 (AI usage counts), 6.4 (new "One row per model attempt, and per image call" bullet), 6.11 Privacy. New tests: Deno `handler.test.ts` (the ok image row checked in full and linked to the description, both rows with the recipe id; an upper-case recipe id is lowercased; the mock image model logs `mock` with no tokens; a refusal, a 500 and a timeout through the real `generateImage` over a fake fetch log `refused`/400, `api_error`/500 and `timeout`/nulls with their errors and bodies; a 5000-char body is cut to 4000; `invalid_output` and no-key `error`; the image bytes and base64 are never in a row; a throwing `logAiCall` doesn't fail a success or a refusal; isFood false and a failed description log no image row), `image.test.ts` (what each error carries, including a non-JSON and an empty body; `imageModelId`). Existing tests I changed because the behavior changed: four handler tests now expect the second `ai_call` step/row; admin `ai-usage.test.ts`'s "status this portal doesn't know" uses `blocked` now that `refused` is known (plus a new ordering test), and its fixtures have `refused: 0`; pgTAP `51_admin_ai_usage` expects `"refused": 0`; `categorize-ingredients/cli.test.ts`'s record helper gets `recipe_id` (type only). pgTAP `06_ai_calls` (25 → 31 tests): `recipe_id` type and nullable, `refused` accepted, `ai_call_stats` counts it with no image fallback, the FK, deleting the recipe nulls `recipe_id`. Checks: Deno generate-recipe-photo (65), categorize-ingredients (308), import-recipe (177), import-recipe-photo (64), match-recipe-steps (61), suggest-recipe-tags (59) pass; every touched `index.ts`, CLI and the photo eval type-check (`deno test --no-run`, since `deno check` needs approval here); `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1634) pass; root jest (5205), lint, tsc pass; admin vitest (140), tsc, lint pass. No real AI calls. The scratch files `.probe/probe.ts` and `supabase/functions/categorize-ingredients/zz-probe.test.ts` from the last task are still there; delete them by hand.

title: Flagged AI calls
text: Flagged AI calls (spec 4.12, 6.11). One SQL function decides what's flagged, `private.ai_call_flag(public.ai_calls) returns text` (immutable): `not_food` for a `recipePhotoDescription` row whose `output->>'isFood'` is `'false'`, `refused` for a `refused` row, `content_filter` for a `content-filter` `finish_reason` (any task), else null. Use it in a partial index for the flagged rows. Spec 6.11: when the description says the recipe isn't food, the call is flagged (it still answers `not_food` and gives the slot back, as now). Add the rule to spec 4.12 beside the portal functions below. Retention: replace the `ai-calls-retention` job's command so a row is deleted after 30 days unless it, or a row whose `fallback_of` is its id, or the row its `fallback_of` points to, is flagged; those go after 180 days (so a refused image keeps the description holding the recipe the user wrote, and the other way round). Deleting the account still nulls `user_id`: no copy of who made it is kept. Update spec 5, 6.4 and 6.5 (and the Privacy lines changed above) to say flagged calls and their linked calls are kept 180 days. pgTAP: each flag case, an `isFood: true` description and an ordinary failure are not flagged; the job's command (run directly) deletes a 31-day-old unflagged row, keeps a 31-day-old flagged row and the row linked to it, and deletes both at 181 days.
notes: Flagged AI calls (2026-10-19, spec 4.12, 6.11): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261122120000_ai_calls_flags.sql`: `private.ai_call_flag(public.ai_calls)` (sql, immutable, revoked from public/anon/authenticated) answers `not_food` (a `recipePhotoDescription` row with `output->>'isFood' = 'false'`), `refused` (status `refused`), `content_filter` (finish reason `content-filter`, any task), else null, checked in that order; partial index `ai_calls_flagged_idx` on `(created_at desc) where private.ai_call_flag(ai_calls) is not null`; plus `ai_calls_fallback_of_idx` (partial, on `fallback_of`) for the retention lookups and the next task's `recovered`/`fallback`. `ai-calls-retention` is rescheduled under the same name (pg_cron replaces the command and keeps `17 3 * * *`): delete after 30 days unless the row, the row its `fallback_of` points to, or a row whose `fallback_of` is its id is flagged; those go after 180 days. User deletion still just nulls `user_id` (unchanged). No app or function code changed: `generate-recipe-photo` already answers `not_food` and releases the slot. Spec: 4.12 new **Flagged AI calls** bullet after AI usage (the portal functions come in the next task); 5 (server-only tables line and the `ai_calls` retention sentence); 6.4 Privacy; 6.5; 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 6.10 and 6.11 Privacy lines say 180 days when flagged or linked; 6.11 step 6 says the `not_food` row is flagged. New pgTAP `54_ai_call_flags` (20 tests): each flag case, `isFood: true`, an ordinary failure and `isFood: false` on another task not flagged, the function is immutable and not callable by `authenticated`, the partial index exists with its predicate; running the job's command from `cron.job` directly: one job with its schedule kept, a 31-day unflagged row deleted, a 29-day row kept, a 31-day refused image kept with its description, a 31-day `not_food` primary kept with the row linking to it, a flagged pair at 181 days both deleted, a 179-day flagged row kept. Checks: `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1654) pass; root jest (5205), lint, tsc pass. No real AI calls. (`/tmp/pbspec/edit.py` is an unused scratch file outside the repo.)

text: Portal functions for failed and flagged AI calls (spec 4.12). Since it shows a user's own text, it writes one `admin.admin_actions` row per call (`action` `view_ai_call`, `target_user_id` the call's user, `details` `{ ai_call_id, task, flag }`, no note, `performed_by` the admin's id, as the plan functions set it), so it isn't `stable`. `admin_user_detail` gains `ai_flags`: the user's flagged calls in the last 30 days, a count per flag. Update spec 4.12 (a bullet after **AI usage**): admins can read any call's instructions, prompt and response, and who made it, and see the AI photos made, in the portal; opening a call is audited. Update the **Activity** bullet's list of what writes `admin_actions`, and spec 5's storage policies.

title: The index card recipe view
text: The index card recipe view (spec 4.5, board F `docs/design/recipe-view/f-index-card.png`). When `useRecipeViewStyle()` is `indexCard`, `src/app/recipe/[id]/index.tsx` renders `RecipeIndexCard` (`src/features/recipes/recipe-index-card.tsx`) in its scroll view in place of the photo header, band, switch and cards; the header's ⋯ menu, the `RecipeActionDock` (with Plan, its toasts and hidden-while-adding), the add bar, the toasts, servings state (`chosen`), the ingredient add/edit/delete/long-press handlers and the Method picks all stay in the screen and are passed in, so both views behave the same. On a plain `background` (no tinted band, header not transparent, `headerStyle` `background`, no shadow), 20 pt side margins: **Top row**: the name in `screenTitle` (`accessibilityRole` header), wrapping, beside a 64 × 64 pt square (`rounded.lg`, cover) at its top right with `spacing.lg` between: the photo (the household's own, else the site's, as now; uploading shows the device's copy) over the recipe's tile colour (`aisles[hue].soft`), which shows alone with no photo, while it loads and if it fails; tapping it opens the Choose a photo sheet (VoiceOver "Add photo" or "Change photo"); while Generate with AI runs, a small spinner in it. The plan badges (`PlanBadges`) under the name. **Source line**: the link's host without `www.` (`recipeLinkParts`) in `aisles[hue].strong` `headline`, opening Safari, then " · " in `inkSecondary`, then "for 4" (`forServingsLabel`, the stepper's servings) in `ink` `headline` with a 2 pt `aisles[hue].soft` underline; tapping "for 4" swaps it for the same `Stepper` (and **Reset** when off the recipe's servings) the Ingredients card has. No link: just the servings; no servings: a dashed **Add servings** pill as now; neither: no line. The link is edited from the standard view only. **Notes**: in `lead` italic, `aisles[hue].strong`, inside curly quotes, all of it (no line limit); tap to edit as the band's notes do; no notes: the "+ Add notes" row as now. Tags aren't shown. A hairline `separator` under that, `spacing.lg` above and below. **Ingredients**, no card, no aisle dots: one row per ingredient, at least `minTapTarget` tall, the amount (`formatAmount`, or scaled to the stepper's servings) right-aligned in `inkSecondary` `body` in a fixed column (the widest amount, measured, capped at 40% of the width) and the name (`displayItemName`, then the note in `inkSecondary`) in `ink` `body`, `spacing.md` between. A row keeps tap to edit, long-press to add to a list (and its VoiceOver action) and swipe left to delete, so factor `RecipeIngredientRow`'s gestures out or give it a `layout` prop rather than copying them. Then "+ Add ingredient" (`AddIngredientRow`). No ingredients: the same empty text as the card. **Method**: with steps, "Method, 8 steps" and a `chevron.right` in `aisles[hue].strong` `headline` (`stepPath`'s count, as the switch counts it); a tap shows the `RecipeMethodCard` under it, with the line turning to "Hide method" and a `chevron.down`, kept while the screen is open (VoiceOver: a button with the expanded state). No steps: the Method card as the standard view shows it with none (its Add steps). The content ends above the dock as now. Strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts`. Jest (`src/features/recipes/__tests__/`): the setting picks the view, and switching it on an open screen swaps the view; the source line with a link and servings, servings only, neither; tapping "for 4" shows the stepper and scales the amounts; the amount column right-aligns; the method line's count, expanding and its VoiceOver state; the photo square's photo, tile colour, and its tap opens the sheet; the dock still shows Add to a list, Cook and Plan. Update spec 4.5's **Recipe view trial** bullet with the layout. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on a simulator, set Settings > Design trials > Recipe view to Index card and open an imported recipe with a photo, one without a photo or link, and one with no steps; compare each with board F, check long-press, swipe delete, add ingredient, the servings stepper, Plan and Cook work, then switch back to Standard with the recipe open.
notes: The index card recipe view (2026-10-19, spec 4.5, board F): DONE, checked off. New `src/features/recipes/recipe-index-card.tsx` (`RecipeIndexCard`, `amountColumnWidth`): the top row (name as a header, plan badges, 64 pt photo square over the tile colour that opens Choose a photo, "Add photo"/"Change photo", a spinner while generating), the source line (host without www., " · ", "For 4" over a 2 pt soft underline that swaps to the Stepper and Reset; servings only; a link with the Add servings pill; neither: no line), the notes (in full, in quotes, `lead` italic, strong tint, tap to edit; "+ Add notes"), a hairline, the ingredient rows (the amount column is measured from unseen copies of each amount, capped at 40% of the rows' width less margins), Add ingredient, and the method line ("Method, N steps" from `stepPath`, chevron, expanded state, "Hide method"), or with no steps the Method card. `src/app/recipe/[id]/index.tsx` reads `useRecipeViewStyle()` and renders it in place of the photo header, band, switch and cards, passing the screen's state and handlers (`chosen`, edit, the add-to-list menu, a new `removeIngredient`, `openAdd`, `ingredientsLayout`, Method picks, photo). The index card's header options are `background`, not transparent, no shadow. `RecipeIngredientRow` gained `layout` (`card` by default, or `indexCard`) and `amountWidth`, so the gestures aren't copied. `AddIngredientRow` moved to `src/features/recipes/add-ingredient-row.tsx`. Strings `recipes.indexCard.{notes,hideMethod,changePhoto}` in en and es (es quotes «»). Spec 4.5's Recipe view trial bullet now describes the layout. Choices I made where the task named things the code doesn't have: there's no `separator` colour token, so the hairline is `border` (DESIGN.md's hairline token); there's no `rounded.lg`, so the square is `rounded.md` (12, like the recipe photo tiles); new size token `recipeIndexPhoto` 64 (theme.ts and DESIGN.md). "for 4" uses `forServingsLabel` as the task says, so it reads "For 4" (board F shows lowercase). With neither a link nor servings there's no line, as the task says, so this view doesn't offer Add servings in that case. Figtree had no italic face (iOS doesn't synthesize one for custom fonts), so app.json's expo-font now embeds Figtree 400 Regular Italic on iOS and Android (needs a rebuild). Tests: new `src/features/recipes/__tests__/recipe-index-card.test.tsx` (29 tests): the setting picks the view, with its header options; switching on an open screen, both ways; servings carry between views; name and square styles; the photo square with no photo, a site photo, a failed photo, and the generating spinner; the source line with a link and servings (styles, underline, opens Safari), servings only, non-link text, a link without servings (the Add servings pill opens the prompt), and neither; "For 4" → the stepper scales the amounts, and Reset; notes in full, in quotes, italic, editing saves and keeps the link, + Add notes, no tags; the hairline; the rows' layout, note colour, no hairline or dot; the amount column right-aligned, measured and capped at 40%; `amountColumnWidth`; tap to edit, the long-press menu, swipe delete with its toast; Add ingredient opens the add bar; the method line's count, chevron, expanding, VoiceOver state, path count with headings, one step, no steps; the dock's Add to a list, Cook and Plan, with and without stepper servings; Spanish. Changed an existing test: the `embeddedWeights` helper in `src/constants/__tests__/theme.test.ts` now counts upright faces only (the task adds an italic file, which it would otherwise count as a second 400), and a new test checks that Figtree 400 italic is the only italic embedded. Checks: jest (5246), lint, tsc pass. No real AI calls. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: see manual-checks.md (The index card recipe view).
